Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 17, verse 45:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[45] ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier.﴾

﴿And when you recite the Qur'an﴾ i.e., to these polytheists. ﴿We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾ i.e., who do not affirm the resurrection and do not acknowledge reward and punishment for deeds: ﴿a hidden barrier﴾ i.e., of ignorance and blindness of the heart. So He veils their hearts from understanding what you recite to them, so that they do not benefit from it, as a punishment from Us for their disbelief.

As for the meaning of the barrier being "hidden" (mastur), i.e., from the eyes, so that their sight does not perceive it. It is related from al-Akhfash that (maf'ul) may come in the sense of (fa'il), as in maymun and mash'um meaning yamin and shA'im (blessed and ill-omened, i.e., one who gives blessing and one who gives omen). Just as (fa'il) may come in the sense of (maf'ul), as in ma' dafiq (a gushing water, i.e., a poured-out water).

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[46] ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears a deafness. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn away in aversion on their backs.﴾

﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾ — i.e., many veils (singular: kinan): ﴿lest they understand it﴾ — i.e., out of aversion to understanding it. ﴿And in their ears a deafness﴾ — i.e., a deafness that prevents them from listening to it. This is what overspreads them of abandonment by God Most High, leaving them unable to comprehend what is recited to them and to listen attentively to it.

Abu al-Su'ud said: These are metaphors expressing the completeness of their ignorance of the affairs of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the extreme aversion of their hearts from the Noble Qur'an, and the rejection of their ears toward it. They were brought as an explanation of their failure to comprehend the glorification of the tongue of speech, following the explanation of their failure to comprehend the glorification of the tongue of state, and as a notice that this glorification is so manifest that one would not depict their lack of understanding of it except due to a strong obstacle that overtakes the senses and nullifies them, as an alert that their present condition is more ugly than their previous condition.

﴿And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an﴾ — i.e., without it being accompanied by mention of anything of their deities: ﴿they turn away in aversion on their backs﴾ — i.e., fleeing from hearing the Oneness (tawhid) of God.

Al-Qashani said: Because of the dispersion of their desires and the scattering of their concern in worshipping their objects of worship, from the kinds of corporeal things and appetites. Thus the meaning of unity does not suit their inner selves, since they are attached to multiplicity and veiled by it.

Then God Most High informed of what the polytheists, the leaders of Quraysh, were conspiring together about, by His words, threatening them:

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[47-48] ﴿We are most knowing of why they listen when they listen to you, and when they confer privately, when the wrongdoers say, "You follow none but a man affected by sorcery."﴾ ﴿See how they strike for you comparisons, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way.﴾ [al-Isra' 17:47-48].

﴿We are most knowing of why they listen﴾: that is, because of what they listen for, namely mockery, belittling, and idle talk. ﴿when they listen to you, and when they confer privately, when the wrongdoers say, "You follow none but a man affected by sorcery"﴾: that is, he has been bewitched, so he has gone mad and his speech has become confused.

﴿See how they strike for you comparisons﴾ [al-Isra' 17:48]: that is, they likened you to the poet, the sorcerer, and the madman. ﴿so they have gone astray﴾ [al-Isra' 17:48]: that is, they have strayed from the truth and guidance because of you. ﴿and cannot find a way﴾ [al-Isra' 17:48]: that is, they cannot find the path of truth, because of their straying from it and their distance from it, and because God has forsaken them so that they do not reach it. Or the meaning is: they cannot find a way to any criticism that anyone could accept; rather, they stumble about in what no one doubts is false, like one bewildered in his affair who does not know what to do.

(p. 3938)

(p. 3938)

The exposition of His words, may He be exalted:

[49-52] ﴿They say, "When we are bones and crumbled dust, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ ﴿Say, "Be stones or iron,"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:50] ﴿"or a creation of what is greater in your breasts."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51] ﴿They will say, "Who will restore us?" Say, "The One who originated you the first time." Then they will shake their heads at you and say, "When will it be?" Say, "It may be soon."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51] ﴿On the Day He calls you, you will respond with His praise and you will think that you remained only a little.﴾ [al-Isra' 17:52]

﴿They say, "When we are bones"﴾, which is what has decayed and crumbled, ﴿"and crumbled dust, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ ﴿Say, "Be stones or iron,"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:50] ﴿"or a creation of what is greater in your breasts."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51] That is: what is greater in your souls than accepting life, and what you suppose to be greater for the Creator to revive. Yet He gives you life, and your resurrection does not overpower Him. So how much more so when you are bones and dust, though you were previously described as living! Something is more acceptable for what is familiar in it than for what is unfamiliar. ﴿They will say﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51], that is, after the proof has become binding upon them: ﴿"Who will restore us?" Say, "The One who originated you the first time." Then they will shake their heads at you﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51], that is, they will move them up and down, in amazement and mockery. ﴿And say, "When will it be?"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51], that is, what you have mentioned of the return. ﴿Say, "It may be soon."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51]

﴿On the Day He calls you, you will respond﴾ [al-Isra' 17:52], that is, on the Day He raises you, you will rise. Al-Qadi said: He used calling and responding metaphorically, to draw attention to their swiftness and the ease of their matter, and that the purpose of both is the summoning for reckoning and recompense. End.

It has also been said that both are literal, as in the verse: ﴿On the Day the caller calls from a near place﴾ [Qaf 50:41]. And in His words ﴿On the Day He calls you﴾ [al-Isra' 17:52] there are aspects noted by the grammarians: such as its being a substitute for ﴿qariban﴾ ("near") on the basis that it is an adverbial expression of time; or being in the accusative governed by ﴿yakunu﴾ ("it will be"), or by an implied verb such as ﴿udhkur﴾ ("remember") or ﴿tub'athun﴾ ("you will be raised"). And His words ﴿with His praise﴾ [al-Isra' 17:52], that is: to Him belongs praise for summoning you for recompense, and His promise is realized in truth. ﴿And you will think that you remained only a little﴾ [al-Isra' 17:52], that is: you will consider the duration of your stay in the graves and resting places to be short, due to your being distracted from that time. Or it refers to the first life, since you will regard it as short in comparison with the Hereafter.

Say, "The One who originated you the first time." Then they will shake their heads at you and say, "When will it be?" Say, "It may be soon."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51] ﴿On the Day He calls you, you will respond with His praise and you will think that you remained only a little.﴾ [al-Isra' 17:52]

﴿They say, "When we are bones"﴾, which is what has decayed and crumbled, ﴿"and crumbled dust, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ ﴿Say, "Be stones or iron,"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:50] ﴿"or a creation of what is greater in your breasts."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51] That is: what is greater in your souls than accepting life, and what you suppose to be greater for the Creator to revive. Yet He gives you life, and your resurrection does not overpower Him. So how much more so when you are bones and dust, though you were previously described as living! Something is more acceptable for what is familiar in it than for what is unfamiliar. ﴿They will say﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51], that is, after the proof has become binding upon them: ﴿"Who will restore us?" Say, "The One who originated you the first time." Then they will shake their heads at you﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51], that is, they will move them up and down, in amazement and mockery. ﴿And say, "When will it be?"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51], that is, what you have mentioned of the return. ﴿Say, "It may be soon."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:51]

﴿On the Day He calls you, you will respond﴾ [al-Isra' 17:52], that is, on the Day He raises you, you will rise. Al-Qadi said: He used calling and responding metaphorically, to draw attention to their swiftness and the ease of their matter, and that the purpose of both is the summoning for reckoning and recompense. End.

It has also been said that both are literal, as in the verse: ﴿On the Day the caller calls from a near place﴾ [Qaf 50:41]. And in His words ﴿On the Day He calls you﴾ [al-Isra' 17:52] there are aspects noted by the grammarians: such as its being a substitute for ﴿qariban﴾ ("near") on the basis that it is an adverbial expression of time; or being in the accusative governed by ﴿yakunu﴾ ("it will be"), or by an implied verb such as ﴿udhkur﴾ ("remember") or ﴿tub'athun﴾ ("you will be raised"). And His words ﴿with His praise﴾ [al-Isra' 17:52], that is: to Him belongs praise for summoning you for recompense, and His promise is realized in truth. ﴿And you will think that you remained only a little﴾ [al-Isra' 17:52], that is: you will consider the duration of your stay in the graves and resting places to be short, due to your being distracted from that time. Or it refers to the first life, since you will regard it as short in comparison with the Hereafter.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[53-54] "And say to My servants that they should speak that which is best. Indeed, Satan incites [discord] among them. Indeed, Satan is ever to mankind a clear enemy. Your Lord is most knowing of you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you; or if He wills, He will punish you. And We have not sent you over them as a guardian."

"And say to My servants" means: those who believe along with you, intending to bring their companions closer to what is right, as in the command of resurrection. "That they should speak" in counsel, "that which is best": that is, they should not be harsh with anyone, nor be careless in speech. "Indeed, Satan incites [discord] among them": that is, he corrupts and stirs up evil and disputation, so that harm falls between them. "Indeed, Satan is ever to mankind a clear enemy."

His words, Exalted is He: "Your Lord is most knowing of you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you; or if He wills, He will punish you" [al-Isra': 54] are addressed to these polytheists of Quraysh. That is: if He wills, He will have mercy upon you, so He will turn to you in His mercy, and you will turn back to Him. And if He wills, He will punish you by forsaking you in faith, so that you die in polytheism, and He will punish you for it on the Day of Resurrection.

His words, Exalted is He: "And We have not sent you over them as a guardian" [al-Isra': 54] means: their affair is not entrusted to you, that you should compel them to faith. Rather, We sent you only as a bearer of good news and a warner, to convey Our messages to them.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[55] ﴿Your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth. And We did prefer some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the Zabur (Psalms).﴾

﴿Your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning that nothing in them is hidden from Him. Necessarily, then, He knows best these (individuals). This contains an indication of His mercy in sending the messengers, given the creation's need for them, and of His will regarding whom He chooses for His message and selects for His prophethood, knowing him to be fit for it. And His exalted words:

﴿And We did prefer some of the prophets over others﴾, meaning: because His knowledge and wisdom required that. For He knows best who is in the heavens and the earth and their conditions. Thus He gave Musa (Moses) the Tawrah (Torah) and spoke to him, and Isa (Jesus) the Injil (Gospel), and Dawud (David) the Zabur (Psalms). He favoured them over others by what He gave them. He gave Muhammad (ﷺ) the Qur'an, and so preferred him by it over all the prophets. And His exalted words, ﴿and We gave David the Zabur﴾, meaning: it comprises wisdom and decisive speech, so We favoured him by it. It has been said: the verse is a rebuttal of them when they deemed it improbable that he (ﷺ) should be a prophet, rather than someone whom they regarded as great among them in wealth and status. He mentioned "those in the heavens" to refute their saying: ﴿Why were the angels not sent down to us?﴾ [al-Furqan: 21], and He mentioned "those on the earth" to refute their saying: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man of the two cities?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31]. The singling out of David for mention is an indication of the preference of the Prophet (ﷺ), as is shown by what was written in it: ﴿that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [al-Anbiya: 105]. So there is an allusion in it to what befell him of being described by what is mentioned in it. Choosing the Zabur over kingship is an explanation of the aspect of his nobility, and that he was (honoured) by what was revealed to him of the Book and knowledge, not by kingship and wealth, so they said. The apparent meaning is that it is an indication that David, peace be upon him, was not, in his early state, among those who would presume that he would attain what he attained in wisdom and kingship, yet Allah singled him out with both and distinguished him over the people of his age. Since that was a divine singling out, it is no wonder that He, glorified is He, should single out from among the Arabs the one who was known to be the most judicious in intellect and the most complete in excellence, for the sealing of prophethood and the guidance of His creation, through His method and His law.

And His exalted words:

(p-٣٩٤١)

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 17, verses 56–57:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He:

[56–57] ﴿Say: "Call upon those you claim besides Him; they do not possess the removal of harm from you, nor its transfer."﴾ ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord, [striving to be] nearest to Him, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared.﴾ [Al-Isra: 57].

﴿Say: "Call upon those you claim besides Him; they do not possess the removal of harm from you, nor its transfer."﴾

﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord, [striving to be] nearest to Him, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared.﴾ [Al-Isra: 57]

That is: Say to these polytheists, who worship besides Allah one whom He created: Call upon those whom you claim to be lords and gods besides Him, when a harm descends upon you, and consider whether they are able to repel that from you or to transfer it from you to others. Then you would call them gods, but they are not able to do that and do not possess it. Rather, the one who possesses and is able to do it is your Creator and their Creator.

Al-Tabari narrated from Ibn Abbas that this verse refers to a people of polytheists who worshipped the Messiah, Uzair and the angels. So Allah informed them that these are His servants, who hope for His mercy, fear His punishment, and draw near to Him through deeds. A parallel to this verse in forbidding that the angels and prophets be associated with Allah, exalted is He, is His saying: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should give him the Scripture and wisdom and prophethood and then he should say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allah." But [he would say], "Be academics of the Lord, by what you have been teaching of the Scripture and what you have been studying."﴾ [Al Imran: 79] and ﴿Nor would He order you to take the angels and prophets as lords. Would He order you to disbelief after you have submitted [to Him]?﴾ [Al Imran: 80] (p-٣٩٤٢). In His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾ [Al-Isra: 57] there is an indication that worship is not complete except with hope and fear. By hope, acts of obedience increase, and by fear, misdeeds decrease. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿to be feared﴾ [Al-Isra: 57] means: it should be guarded against and one should fear its descent. We seek refuge in Allah from it. And His saying, exalted is He:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[58] ﴿And there is no town but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection, or punish it with a severe punishment. That is written in the Book as a decree.﴾

﴿And there is no town but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection, or punish it with a severe punishment. That is written in the Book as a decree.﴾

This is information that He has decreed and determined: that there is no town whose people rebel against their prophet except that He will annihilate them, or bring upon them a punishment of severe intensity. This is because of their sins, their wrongdoings, and their failure to respond to their prophet, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾ [Hud: 101], and He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss﴾ [al-Talaq: 9], and He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers﴾ [al-Talaq: 8], and so on. And His, Exalted is He, words:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 17, verse 59:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[59] ﴿And We do not withhold from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We do not send the signs except as a warning.﴾

﴿And We do not withhold from sending the signs﴾, i.e., those that Quraysh propose: ﴿except that the former peoples denied them﴾ (p-3943), i.e., except that the denial of the former peoples, who are like them, such as ʿAd and Thamud, prevented it. And had they been sent, they would have denied them with the same denial as those. Thus they would have deserved annihilation (istiʾsal), according to the divine custom (al-sunnah al-ilahiyyah) that has prevailed. We have decided that We would not annihilate them, because among them are those who will believe, or who will beget those who believe. Then He mentioned some of the nations destroyed for denying the proposed signs, so He said: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel﴾, i.e., We gave the people of Salih the she-camel in response to their request: ﴿as a visible sign﴾, i.e., a clear proof, through its evidence making the blind see: ﴿but they wronged her﴾, i.e., they disbelieved in her and wronged themselves by slaughtering her, so Allah destroyed them to the last of them and took vengeance upon them. ﴿And We do not send the signs except as a warning﴾, i.e., We do not send the proposed signs except as a warning to people, so that they may know the divine custom concerning the obstinate, and thus remember and repent.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The people of Mecca asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to turn al-Safa into gold for them and to remove the mountains from them so that they could cultivate. He was told: 'If you wish, you may give them respite; and if you wish, what they asked for will come to them, but if they disbelieve, they will be destroyed as I destroyed the nations before them.' He said: 'No, rather I will give them respite,' and Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And We do not withhold from sending﴾ the verse." Al-Nasa'i also narrated it.

[The commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:]

[60] ﴿And [remember] when We told you, "Surely your Lord encompasses the people. And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and [did not make] the cursed tree in the Qur'an [except as a trial]. We warn them, but it only increases them in great transgression."﴾

﴿And [remember] when We told you, "Surely your Lord encompasses the people"﴾ That is, by knowledge, so nothing of their disbelief and denial is hidden from Him. Among what happened from them, after the vision and the report about the tree, was denial, mockery and idle talk. As He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people.﴾ Most scholars said: it means what the Prophet (ﷺ) saw on the night of the Isra' (the night journey) of the signs. When the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned it to the people, some of them denied it and called it a lie. God made that a source of steadfastness and certainty for the sincere believers. So it became a trial, that is, a test and an examination. Whoever held that the Isra' was a dream relied on this, since the word "vision" is specific to dreams. It is answered that His words, exalted is He, ﴿except as a trial for the people﴾ refute this, because no one is tested by a dream and calls it a lie. In the language, "ru'ya" (vision) is used in the sense of seeing in general, and this is its literal meaning. It was said: it is literally used for both dream-vision and waking vision at night. Al-Suhayli (al-Suhayli, a scholar of the Qur'an and grammar) mentioned that it occurs in the speech of the Arabs with this meaning, and that it is like "qurba" and "qurba" (nearness). It was said: it is a metaphor, either by way of mushakalah (conforming the expression to what precedes it) because they called it a vision, or it runs according to their claim, or by way of comparison to it because of what it contains of breaking habit, or because it happened at night, or because of its speed. This was reported by al-Shihab (al-Shihab al-Khafaji, a commentator).

Al-Tabari (al-Tabari, the historian and exegete) narrated from al-Hasan (al-Basri) regarding this verse; he said: "He (ﷺ) was taken on the night journey in the evening to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), and he prayed in it, and God showed him what He showed him of the signs. Then he woke up in Makkah, and he informed them that he had been taken on the night journey to Bayt al-Maqdis. They said to him: 'O Muhammad! What is your matter? You spent the evening in it and then in the morning you were among us, telling us that you went to Bayt al-Maqdis?' They were amazed at that, to the point that some of them apostatized from Islam."

Others said: the verse is about his (ﷺ) vision in which he saw that he would enter Makkah. Al-Barri (al-Barri, a commentator) narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "It is said that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was shown that he and his companions had entered Makkah, while he was that day in Madinah. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) hastened the journey to Makkah before the appointed time, and the polytheists turned him back. Some people said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has been turned back, and he had told us that he would enter it.' So his return was their trial. That was the year of al-Hudaybiyah. Then he entered Makkah the following year." And God, mighty and majestic is He, revealed: ﴿Certainly God has fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth﴾ (al-Fath: 27).

It cannot be said that the surah is Makkan while the story of al-Hudaybiyah is after the Hijrah (emigration to Madinah), because it is possible that he saw that vision in Makkah, and this verse was revealed to him. But he mentioned it in the year of al-Hudaybiyah because at that time he was in Makkah. So it was known that his entry was after his departure from it. This is what was said.

Some scholars went to the view that many Makkan surahs had Madani verses added to them, as in al-Itqan (al-Itqan, by al-Suyuti). Al-Tabari preferred the first view, in agreement with most scholars. We have mentioned many times that the salaf (the early generations of scholars) may mean by their saying "this verse was revealed about such-and-such" that the wording of the verse includes that matter, not that it was literally the cause of its revelation. In light of this, there is no difficulty.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾ are a conjunction to "the vision." Most scholars hold that it is the tree of al-Zaqqum, mentioned in Surah al-Saffat in His words: ﴿Is that better as a welcome, or the tree of al-Zaqqum?﴾ (al-Saffat: 62) ﴿Surely We made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾ (al-Saffat: 63) ﴿Surely it is a tree that springs from the root of Hellfire﴾ (al-Saffat: 64) ﴿Its fruit is as if it were the heads of devils﴾ (al-Saffat: 65), and the verses that follow. Their trial regarding it is what al-Tabari narrated from Ibn Abbas and Qatadah: that Abu Jahl said: "Your companion here claims, meaning the Prophet, may God's blessings be upon him, that in the Fire there is a tree, and the Fire consumes trees!" So they denied that. In another narration: Abu Jahl said: "Does he frighten me with the tree of al-Zaqqum?" Then he called for dates and butter and began eating and saying: "Eat zaqqum (tazaqqamu)! We do not know al-Zaqqum except as this." The meaning of its being cursed in the Qur'an is: the cursing of the one who eats it in it, on the basis that this is a metaphor in the attribution. Or "cursed" means "harmful," because it boils in the bellies like the boiling of hamim (scalding water). So it is either a mursal (general) metaphor or an isti'arah (metaphor).

His words, exalted is He, ﴿and We warn them﴾ mean: with that and with its like of the signs. ﴿But it only increases them﴾ that is, the warning: ﴿in great transgression﴾ that is, persistence in the misguidance and disbelief they are in.

(p-3946) Al-Mahayimi (al-Mahayimi, a commentator) said: That is, if We sent to them the signs they proposed, they would say: "He is more great than whoever surrounds the gates of magic." So there is no benefit in sending them except to hasten the worldly punishment. But that would contradict the manifestation of His religion over all religion.

Then God, exalted is He, pointed out that this transgression is from following Satan, and that he and his party are, because of their obstinacy and rebellion against the truth, in the Fire, by His words, glorified is He:

The commentary on His saying, the Exalted:

[61-62] ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis. He said, "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Tell me, is this the one You have honored over me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize control of his descendants, except for a few."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:62].

﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾ means: as a greeting and an honoring. ﴿They prostrated, except Iblis. He said, "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ As He said in another verse: ﴿"I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ [al-A'raf 7:12].

﴿He said﴾ [al-Isra' 17:62] means: with audacity toward the Lord and disbelief in Him: ﴿"Tell me, is this the one You have honored over me?"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:62] means: inform me about this one whom You honored over me by commanding me to prostrate to him; why did You honor him over me? Or the meaning is: inform me, is this the one You have honored over me, ﴿"If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize control of his descendants, except for a few"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:62], meaning: I will blind them and destroy them through misguidance, except the sincere ones.

The discussion of the words of His saying (Exalted is He):

[63-65] ﴿He said, "Go! Whoever among them follows you, then indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense."﴾ ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, and urge upon them your horsemen and your foot-soldiers, and share with them in wealth and children, and make promises to them. But Satan promises them nothing except delusion.﴾ [Al-Isra: 64] ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them. And sufficient is your Lord as Guardian.﴾ [Al-Isra: 65]

﴿He said, "Go!"﴾ That is: proceed to your business which you have chosen. ﴿Whoever among them follows you, then indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense﴾: that is, a complete recompense.

﴿And incite﴾ [Al-Isra: 64]: that is, provoke and disturb. ﴿Whomever you can among them﴾ [Al-Isra: 64]: that is, whom you are able to provoke so as to deceive. ﴿With your voice﴾ [Al-Isra: 64]: that is, with your call to corruption. He expressed the call by "voice" to belittle it, as if it had no meaning. ﴿And urge upon them your horsemen and your foot-soldiers﴾ [Al-Isra: 64]: that is, shout at them. From al-jalaba (with fatha on the letters), which is shouting. And "al-khayl" (the horsemen) means the riders of horses, that is, the mounted riders, metaphorically; the original meaning of "khayl" is steeds. "Al-rajil" (foot-soldiers) is a collective noun for "rajil" (one on foot), the opposite of "faris" (horseman), and what is meant is helpers and followers in general.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, "What is the meaning of Iblis inciting with his voice and urging with his horsemen and foot-soldiers?" Otherwise, if he is immersed in sensory preoccupations, sunk into worldly affairs, Satan shares with him in his wealth and children, by inciting him to associate others with God in love, loving them as one loves God, and adorning for him the enjoyment of them, the multiplication and boasting through their existence, wishing him vain wishes and decorating for him empty hopes. Then Allah, exalted is He, made clear some of the signs of His oneness and divinity by His saying:

Discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[66] ﴿Your Lord is the One who drives the ships for you through the sea, that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed, He is ever Merciful to you.﴾

﴿Your Lord is the One who drives the ships for you through the sea﴾ i.e., He makes the boats sail for you in the sea. ﴿That you may seek of His bounty﴾ i.e., of His provision. The verse is explicit about sailing the sea for trade. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Merciful to you﴾ in that He facilitated for you the means of that.

Abu al-Su'ud said: This is a reminder of some of the blessings which are among the proofs of tawhid (divine oneness), and a preparation for mentioning their monotheism at the touch of harm, as a completion of what passed of His saying: ﴿So they do not possess [the power]﴾ [al-Isra': 56], and the verse, and that is His saying, exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 17, verse 67:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[67] ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke disappear except for Him. But when He brings you safely to land, you turn away. And mankind is ever ungrateful.﴾

﴿And when harm touches you at sea﴾ i.e., the fear of drowning. ﴿those whom you invoke disappear except for Him﴾ i.e., all those whom you call upon and worship vanish from your thoughts and imaginations, except Him alone, for you do not remember anyone else. This is the innate disposition (fitrah) upon which God created creation.

This verse is among those by which one may derive evidence for returning to the sound innate disposition. Many of the principles (usul) have been derived from it, as is known from the words of the scholars (a'immah) on various issues, such as the existence of the Creator and His exaltedness, the Resurrection (ma'ad), and others. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿When He brings you safely﴾ i.e., from drowning, ﴿to land, you turn away﴾ i.e., from monotheism (tawhid), ﴿and mankind is ever ungrateful﴾ i.e., for the blessings of God. The clause serves as a reason for the turning away. Al-Shihab said: "In it there is subtlety, in that He turns away from addressing them specifically, and mentions that the nature of mankind is inclined to this." When they turned away, God turned away from them. Then, exalted is He, He warned them of His great power, with His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion of the words of the Exalted:

[68–69] "Do you then feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you, or send against you a squall of stones, then you will find for yourselves no guardian? Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time and send against you a violent wind and drown you for what you disbelieved, then you will find for yourselves against Us no pursuer?" [al-Isra' 17:69]

"Do you then feel secure that He will cause the side of the land to swallow you": i.e., He will sink it with you in it. "Or send against you a squall of stones": i.e., a wind that pelts you with pebbles, stoning you with them, which would be more severe upon you than drowning. "Then you will find for yourselves no guardian": i.e., no one who would take it upon himself to turn that away from you.

"Or do you feel secure that He will return you to it": i.e., He will strengthen your motives for boarding the sea. "Another time, and send against you a violent wind": i.e., a fierce wind that does not pass by anything without breaking it, so it shatters the ship in the middle of the sea. "And drown you for what you disbelieved, then you will find for yourselves against Us no pursuer": i.e., no one who would demand an account for what We have done, like one who demands retribution against someone other than Us for a drowning. This is like His saying: "and He does not fear its consequence" [al-Shams 91:15].

The discussion of the words of God Most High:

﴿And We have certainly honored the children of Adam, and carried them on the land and the sea, and provided for them of the good things, and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [marked] preference.﴾

﴿And We have certainly honored the children of Adam⌋ — that is, with speech, discernment, reason, knowledge, the [fine] form, and dominion over what is on the earth and the enjoyment of it. ﴿And carried them on the land and the sea⌋ — that is, We facilitated for them the means of livelihood and of the return [to Us], by their traveling in search of them in both, and obtaining them. ﴿And provided for them of the good things⌋ — that is, the varieties of pleasant things that none of the other created beings were provided with. ﴿And preferred them over much of what We have created, with [marked] preference⌋ — that is, a great preference. Therefore it is incumbent upon them to be thankful for these blessings, by worshipping the One who bestowed them alone, and establishing His laws and limits.

Note:

The apparent sense of God's words "over much of" (ʿalā kathīr) is that there are some [beings] over whom mankind was not preferred. It has been said: they are the sanctified essences of the higher assembly, meaning the angels.

Al-Qashani said: As for the superiority of some people, such as the prophets over the favored angels, it is not by virtue of their being children of Adam, but by virtue of the secret deposited in them, alluded to in His words: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know⌋ [al-Baqarah: 30], which is the perfect divine knowledge prepared for that group. In this respect, such a person is not, in that regard, a child of Adam, as it has been said:

"Though I am, in form, a son of Adam, within me there is a meaning that witnesses to my fatherhood."

Some have interpreted "much" (al-kathīr) as "all" (al-kull), just as "little" (al-qalīl) was interpreted as "none" (al-ʿadam) in His words: ﴿so little is it that they believe⌋ [al-Baqarah: 88]. The meaning is: We preferred them over a vast multitude of Our creation, that is, all created beings.

Al-Qashani said: Here "min" (from) is for specification and for emphasis in magnifying it, by describing those over whom [mankind] is preferred as numerous, and by indefinite phrasing of the description and placing it before the described noun. That is: many, and what a multitude — it is all of Our creation, since "min" indicates generality. It is not hidden that preferring one genus over another genus does not necessarily entail preferring each individual of the one over each individual of the other. This matter is well known in the books of kalam.

And the words of God Most High:

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[71-72] "On the Day We shall summon every people with their leader. Whoever is given his record in his right hand—those will read their record, and they will not be wronged the least bit (fatila). And whoever was blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray in way."

"On the Day We shall summon every people with their leader" — i.e., with those whom they followed (ii'tamma bihi) of a prophet, or a leading figure in religion, or a book, or a religion. It will be said: "O followers of so-and-so! O people of such-and-such a religion and such-and-such a book!" It was also said: "with the book of their deeds," so it will be said: "O companions of the book of good!" and "O companions of the book of evil!" They said: There is in this an honor for the people of hadith, because their leader is the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Al-Qashani said: That is, We will bring forward every group of the nations together with their witness who attends them and whom they turn toward and recognize, whether it be the form of a prophet they believed in, or a leader they followed, or a religion or a book, or whatever you wish. [This is] on the reading that the bā' (in bi-imāmihim) means "with" (ma'a). Or We will attribute them to their leader and call them by his name, because he is the one who dominated them and their affair, his love for them prevailing over all their other loves.

Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, preferred the view that the imam is the book of deeds, citing His saying: "And We have enumerated everything in a clear record (imam mubin)" [Ya-Sin: 12], and His saying: "And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it" [al-Kahf: 49], up to the verse, and His saying: "And you will see every nation kneeling; every nation will be called to its record: 'Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.' This is Our record; it speaks against you with truth. Indeed, We used to have transcribed what you were doing" [al-Jathiyah: 28-29]. What he, may Allah have mercy on him, preferred is the correct view, because the Qur'an explains one part of itself by another, and the first thing that should be given attention in the meanings of verses is returning to their parallels.

His saying "Whoever is given" — i.e., from among these summoned ones — "his record" — i.e., the record of his deeds — "in his right hand, those will read their record" — i.e., joyfully and exultantly because of the righteous deeds in it — "and they will not be wronged the least bit (fatila)" — i.e., they will not have their rewards diminished by even a fatil, which is what is in the split of a date-stone, or what one twists between two fingers, or is the least thing; the fatil is a metaphor for paucity, like His saying: "and they will not be wronged at all" [Maryam: 60].

"And whoever was blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray in way" — i.e., whoever was blind in this worldly life to guidance toward the truth will be blind in the Hereafter, not seeing the path of salvation, and more astray in way than he was in this world; for in this life he has faculties, tools and means by which he can be guided. He is in the station of acquisition with his capacity for preparation still intact, but none of that remains there.

It was said: blindness is literal regarding one who cannot perceive visible things due to a defect of his sense, and figurative regarding blindness of insight, which is failure to be guided to the path of salvation. It was also said: it is literal in both senses. On this basis it was permitted that the second "blind" be an elative (af'al al-tafdil), because it is from blindness of the heart, not blindness of sight. It is permissible also to form the elative from inward defects, like "the most foolish" (al-ahmaq) and "the most dull" (al-ablah).

A subtle point:

Al-Nasir said: This verse may be the counterpart (qasima) of the first. That is: whoever is given his book in his right hand, he is the one who sees it and reads it. And whoever was blind in the world, not seeing within himself nor looking toward his return, he is likewise in the Hereafter, not seeing in his book, but rather blind to it, or more blind than he was in the world, according to the two differing interpretations. And His saying, Exalted is He:

"And whoever was blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray in way" — i.e., whoever was blind in this worldly life to guidance toward the truth will be blind in the Hereafter, not seeing the path of salvation, and more astray in way than he was in this world; for in this life he has faculties, tools and means by which he can be guided. He is in the station of acquisition with his capacity for preparation still intact, but none of that remains there.

It was said: blindness is literal regarding one who cannot perceive visible things due to a defect of his sense, and figurative regarding blindness of insight, which is failure to be guided to the path of salvation. It was also said: it is literal in both senses. On this basis it was permitted that the second "blind" be an elative (af'al al-tafdil), because it is from blindness of the heart, not blindness of sight. It is permissible also to form the elative from inward defects, like "the most foolish" (al-ahmaq) and "the most dull" (al-ablah).

A subtle point:

Al-Nasir said: This verse may be the counterpart (qasima) of the first. That is: whoever is given his book in his right hand, he is the one who sees it and reads it. And whoever was blind in the world, not seeing within himself nor looking toward his return, he is likewise in the Hereafter, not seeing in his book, but rather blind to it, or more blind than he was in the world, according to the two differing interpretations. And His saying, Exalted is He:

(p-3954)

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[73-74] ﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you, to fabricate against Us other than it; and then they would have taken you as an intimate friend. And if We had not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little.﴾

This is a report of His, exalted is He, confirming His Messenger, may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon him, and strengthening him, protecting him, taking charge of his affair and guarding him. The polytheists, due to their great variety of harmful methods, their severe obstinacy and the firmness of their resolve, almost tempted him. But it was the care and protection of Allah that kept his foot firm in such a station in calling to Allah, a station in which no one else could remain steady.

It has been narrated that the Thaqif said: "We will not believe until you give us qualities by which we may boast over the Arabs: we shall not bow in prayer, we shall not break our idols with our own hands, and you shall grant us Al-Lat for a year without our having to worship it. If you fear that the Arabs will hear, [and say], 'Why did you give them what you did not give us?', then say: 'Allah commanded me to do so.'"

And it has been narrated that the Quraysh said: "We will not leave you, O Muhammad, to touch the Black Stone until you touch our gods." And they also said: "We will believe in you if you touch our gods."

Imam al-Tabari said: It is possible that the temptation refers to what has been mentioned, and it is possible that it refers to something other than that. There is no clarification in the Book or in any report that settles the matter as to which of these it was. The most correct position is to affirm the apparent meaning until there comes what makes submission to it obligatory, by clarifying what was meant by it.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the speech is: "They almost tempted you." The light (an) [in ﴿إنْ﴾] is the lightened form of the heavy (inna), and the (lam) [in ﴿لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ﴾] is for emphasis. The meaning is: the matter was close to them tempting you, that is, deceiving you and diverting you from the Qur'an, that is, from its ruling. This is because giving them what they asked for would have been opposing the ruling of the Qur'an. His saying ﴿لِتَفْتَرِيَ عَلَيْنا غَيْرَهُ﴾ means: other than what We revealed to you, which is their saying: "Say, Allah commanded me to do so." ﴿وإذًا لاتَّخَذُوكَ خَلِيلا﴾ means: had you done what they wanted, they would have taken you as an intimate friend, and shown the people that you agree with them in their disbelief and are content with their polytheism. Then He said: ﴿ولَوْلا أنْ ثَبَّتْناكَ﴾ means: upon the truth, by Our protecting you; ﴿لَقَدْ كِدْتَ تَرْكَنُ إلَيْهِمْ﴾ means: you would have inclined toward them; ﴿شَيْئًا قَلِيلا﴾. His saying ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ is an expression for the verbal noun, or it means a slight inclination.

It is reported on the authority of Qatadah: "When this verse was revealed, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: 'O Allah, do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye.'"

Then He threatened him in this regard with the most severe threat, saying:

**The Interpretation of His, Exalted is He, Words:**

﴿Then We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death; then you would not find for yourself any helper against Us.﴾

﴿Then We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death.﴾ That is, double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death, meaning the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. "Ḍiʿf" (double, multiple) is an expression for adding to a thing another like it. The punishment is implied by the description of it as "double" in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿Our Lord, whoever sent this forward for us, then increase him in punishment double in the Fire﴾ [Ṣād: 61], and He said: ﴿For each there is double, but you do not know﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 38].

The reason for doubling the punishment is that the kinds of Allah's blessings upon the prophets are more numerous, so their sins are greater, and the punishment deserved for them is therefore greater. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, her punishment will be doubled twofold﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 30].

**Notes:**

**First:** Al-Qaffāl (may Allah have mercy on him), after mentioning what has been narrated concerning the occasion of its revelation, which we have already presented, said: It is also possible to interpret it without restricting it to a specific occasion of revelation, because it is well known that the polytheists used to strive to nullify the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by every means they could. At one time they would say: "If you worship our gods, we will worship your God." So Allah revealed: ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 1], ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 2], and His saying: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam: 9]. They offered him great wealth and beautiful women so that he would abandon his claim to prophethood, so Allah revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾ [Ṭāhā: 131]. They urged him to drive away the believers from himself, so Allah revealed His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾ [al-Anʿām: 52]. Thus it is possible that these verses were revealed in this context, for they intended to tempt him away from his religion and to turn him aside from his path. So Allah, exalted is He, made clear that He would keep him firm upon the upright religion and the straight path. On this understanding, there is no need, in explaining these verses, for anything from those narrations. And Allah knows best.

**Second:** Al-Qāḍī said: The meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had We not made you firm﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 74], and the rest of the verse, is that you were close to inclining toward them, because of the strength of their deception and the severity of their cunning. But Our protection reached you, so you were prevented from coming near to inclining, let alone actually inclining toward them. This is explicit that he (peace and blessings be upon him) did not intend to comply with them, despite the strength of the incentive toward it, and it is evidence that protection comes through Allah's enabling and preservation.

**Third:** Al-Zamakhsharī said: In mentioning the slight inclination and its minimization, together with the severe threat of doubled punishment in both abodes, there is clear evidence that an ugly act becomes more grievously ugly in proportion to the greatness of the status of its doer and the elevation of his rank. It also shows that even the slightest flattery of the deviators is opposition to Allah and departure from His guardianship, and a cause that necessitates His anger and retribution. Therefore, when a believer recites this verse, he should kneel before it and reflect upon it, for it is worthy of reflection, and the one who considers it should feel awe and increase in steadfastness in the religion of Allah.

**Fourth:** There occurs in (Ḥawāshī Jāmiʿ al-Bayān) what is, in its exact wording, as follows: Among the great benefits in this verse is that it is not permissible to leave places of shirk standing once one is able to demolish and nullify them. For they are the symbols of disbelief and polytheism, and they are the greatest of evils, so it is by no means permissible to allow them to remain while one has the power to remove them. The same ruling applies to the shrines built over graves that have been taken as idols and idols worshipped besides Allah. The stones that are sought for veneration, blessing, vows, and kissing: it is not permissible to leave any of them on the face of the earth while one has the power to remove them. Many of them are in the same position as al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt the third, the other, and they are the greatest shirk in their vicinity and by means of them. For al-Lāt, according to what Ibn Khuzaymah transmitted from Mujāhid, was a man who used to knead sawīq (a porridge of roasted grain) for them, and then he died. So they clung to his grave, worshipping him and venerating him. They did not say that al-Lāt created the heavens and the earth. Rather, their polytheism toward al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt the third, the other, was exactly like the polytheism of the people of shirk among the masters of shrines: making vows to them, associating others with them, rubbing against them, kissing them, and touching them. They sought from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) nothing but mere contact with their gods, as they said: "We will believe in you if you touch our gods." And they sought from him nothing but enjoyment of al-Lāt for a year without worship. So he was threatened with this severe warning and firm menace, that he would be punished if he were to incline toward them. The greatest calamity is what has befallen the grave-worshippers of this age, for they have not left undone anything that the pre-Islamic ignorance used to do with idols except that they have done it with graves. ﴿Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return﴾ [al-Baqarah: 156]. Rather, many of them, when an oath is directed at them by their opponent, swear by Allah falsely, and when they are then told: "Swear by your shaykh, or by your belief in the saint so-and-so," they hesitate, refuse, and admit the truth. This is among the clearest evidence that their polytheism has exceeded the polytheism of those who said: "the third of three" [al-Mā'idah: 73]. So, O scholars of religion! And O rulers of the Muslims! What affliction to Islam is more severe than disbelief? What trial to this religion is more harmful to it than worshipping other than Allah? What calamity that Muslims suffer equals this? What evil must be denounced if denouncing this manifest polytheism is not obligatory?

So, O Allah! Grant victory to whoever supports the truth, and guide us to the even path. (End.)

The discourse of God Most High:

[76-77] ﴿And indeed they almost sought to unsettle you from the land to expel you from it; and then they would not have remained after you except for a little while.﴾ ﴿[This was] the way of those We sent before you of Our messengers; and you will not find in Our way any change.﴾ [al-Isra' 17:77]

﴿And indeed they almost﴾ i.e., the people of Makkah: ﴿sought to unsettle you from the land﴾ i.e., they would drive you out with their enmity from Makkah: ﴿to expel you from it; and then they would not have remained after you﴾ i.e., were you to leave, they would not remain after your departure: ﴿except for a little while﴾ i.e., for a short time.

﴿[This was] the way of those We sent before you of Our messengers﴾ [al-Isra' 17:77] meaning: every people who expelled their messenger from among them, then God's way was to destroy them. ﴿Sunnah﴾ is put in the accusative as an emphatic infinitive (maf'ul mutlaq), i.e., God established this as a way (sunnah). ﴿And you will not find in Our way any change﴾ [al-Isra' 17:77] i.e., any alteration. It is not hidden that the meaning of their not remaining is their destruction, whether by uprooting or otherwise.

Ibn Kathir said: And so it happened, for after the hardship of their harm to him became severe, the Prophet (ﷺ) remained among them for only a year and a half after his migration (hijrah) from among them, until God brought them together with him at Badr without prior appointment. He enabled him over them, gave him power over them, and granted him victory over them. He killed their nobles and took captive their chiefs. For this reason God Most High said: ﴿[This was] the way of those We sent﴾ [al-Isra' 17:77], i.e., such is Our custom with those who disbelieved in Our messengers and harmed them: the messenger goes out from among them and the punishment comes upon them. Had the Prophet (ﷺ) not been the messenger of mercy, there would have come upon them from retribution in this world what no one could withstand, as God Most High said: ﴿But God would not punish them while you are among them﴾ [al-Anfal 8:33].
