And the discourse of God Most High:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[78] ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and the recitation of dawn. Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.﴾

When Exalted is He mentioned earlier the plotting of the polytheists and their attempt to drive him out of the land, He commanded him to seek help through establishing the prayers, devoting himself to the worship of Exalted is He, and turning to Him in supplication to repel their plotting and scheming and to be aided against them. Similar to this is His saying: ﴿And We certainly know that your breast is distressed by what they say﴾ [al-Hijr: 97] ﴿So glorify the praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate﴾ [al-Hijr: 98]. And His saying: ﴿So be patient over what they say and glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night glorify Him, and at the ends of the day, that you may be pleased﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130]. And His saying: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45]. This is in terms of the arrangement of the verse with what precedes it.

As for its meaning, His saying ﴿at the decline of the sun﴾ means at its declining (zawal, the moment after the zenith). Ibn Taymiyyah said: "Duluk" is the declining (zawal) according to most of the early scholars (salaf), and this is the correct view. The lam here is for specifying the time, meaning the marking of the time, in the sense of "after," and it may also mean "at." It has also been said that the lam is for causation, since the entry of the time is the cause for the obligation of the prayer. As for ﴿the darkness of the night﴾, it is the gathering of the night and its darkness. As for ﴿the recitation of dawn﴾, it is the Dawn Prayer (Subh). It was called "recitation" (qur'an) because the recitation is one of its pillars (rukn), just as it was called bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujud). This is the naming of the whole by the name of its important part. It thus indicates clearly the obligation of recitation in it, and in other prayers by implication from the text and by analogy. The meaning of ﴿witnessed﴾ is that it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the day: these descend and those ascend, so it is at the end of the record of the night and the beginning of the record of the day. Or it is witnessed by many of those who pray, as is customary; and it is fitting that it be witnessed by a large congregation. Most scholars hold that His saying ﴿and the recitation of dawn﴾ [p. 3960] is in the accusative by coordination with (the prayer), meaning: "and establish the Dawn Prayer." Some grammarians permitted its accusative as an incitement (ighra'), meaning: "and upon you the recitation of dawn," or "adhere to it."

Notes:

First: This verse comprises the five obligatory prayers and their times. The declining of the sun encompasses Zuhr and 'Asr in a single expression, and the darkness of the night encompasses Maghrib and 'Isha' in a single expression. The recitation of dawn is a single prayer that is not combined with another nor shortened. It has been said: this implies that "duluk" is shared between Zuhr and 'Asr, and "ghasaq" is shared between Maghrib and 'Isha', and thus indicates the permissibility of combining (jam') in general between the first two, and likewise between the last two. The answer: it is so, by the excuse of travel, rain, or the like. As for other than these, it is not permitted, because of what the Sunnah has clarified concerning performing each prayer in its specific time, except with an excuse. The hafiz Ibn Kathir said: The Sunnah has clarified, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by continuous transmission (tawatur) of his deeds and sayings, the details of these times as the people of Islam hold today, which they have received from one generation to another, century after century, as is established in its proper places.

Al-'Allamah Abu al-Su'ud said: The intent is not to establish them continuously between the two times, but to establish each prayer in its time that was specified for it by the explanation of Jibril, peace be upon him, just as the number of rak'ahs of each prayer is entrusted to his (ﷺ) explanation. Perhaps the sufficiency with clarifying the beginning and end of the prayer times without separating them is because a person is awake between these times, so some of them are connected to others. This differs from the beginning of the time of 'Isha' and Fajr, for when one is occupied with sleep between them, one of them is cut off from the other. For this reason the time of Fajr was separated from the rest of the times. End of quotation.

Apparently the basis of those who permit combining in residence in general is this verse together with the report from Ibn 'Abbas.

In "Rahmat al-Ummah" there occurs, in substance: It is related from Ibn Sirin that combining is permitted without fear or sickness, for a need, so long as one does not make it a habit. Ibn al-Mundhir and a group chose the permissibility of combining in residence without fear, rain, or sickness. End of quotation.

[p. 3961] The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) prayed in Madinah seven and eight: the Zuhr and the 'Asr, and the Maghrib and the 'Isha'."

In a narration of Muslim: "He prayed Zuhr and 'Asr together, and Maghrib and 'Isha' together, without fear or travel." Many narrators understood this as applying to a rainy night. The matter is well known.

Second: We have said that this verse is one of the verses that gathered the five prayers. Among them is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾ [Hud: 114]. The first end is the Dawn Prayer, for the Dawn Prayer falls within the day, since the fasting person fasts the day, and he fasts from the break of dawn. The Witr is prayed at night, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The prayer of the night is in pairs, two by two; so if you fear the morning, pray one rak'ah as Witr." When it is said "midday" (nisf al-nahar), the intended meaning is the day that begins from the rising of the sun. This is in this subject; and the word "day" (nahar) is intended sometimes from the break of dawn and sometimes from the rising of the sun. But His saying, ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾ [Hud: 114], is intended without doubt from the break of dawn, because after the rising of the sun there is no obligatory prayer for the Muslims, nor even a recommended one. Rather, prayer at the very beginning of sunrise is forbidden until the sun rises high. Whether prayer is recommended at the time of ḍuḥā or is not recommended except for a passing reason is a matter of dispute, and this is not its place. Thus it is known that by the first end He meant from the break of dawn. As for the second end, [p. 3962] it is from the declining (zawal) until sunset. So He made the prayer at this time a prayer of the second end and combined the two within it. Then He said: ﴿and at the approaches of the night﴾ [Hud: 114], and He summarized Maghrib and 'Isha' in "approaches of the night," which are hours of the night. So the times here are three.

And He said, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those among you who have not reached puberty ask permission of you three times: before the Dawn Prayer, and when you put off your clothing at noon, and after the 'Isha' prayer﴾ [al-Nur: 58]. He mentioned Fajr, mentioned Zuhr, and mentioned the 'Isha' prayer. So from midday to after the 'Isha' prayer there are two times for prayer, and He mentioned the first of this period and the last of this period. He also indicated the times in other verses, such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So glory be to Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning﴾ [al-Rum: 17], ﴿And to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you enter the afternoon and at noon﴾ [al-Rum: 18]. Thus it is clarified that for Him is the glorification and praise in the heavens and the earth at evening, at morning, in the afternoon, and at the time of manifestation. So "evening" (masa') encompasses Maghrib and 'Isha', "morning" (sabah) encompasses Fajr, "afternoon" ('ashi) encompasses 'Asr, and "manifestation" (idhar) encompasses Zuhr.

And He said, Exalted is He: ﴿So glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night glorify Him, and at the ends of the day﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130]. And in the other verse: ﴿before the rising of the sun and before the setting﴾ [Qaf: 39], ﴿and during the night glorify Him, and after the prostrations﴾ [Qaf: 40]. So "before the rising of the sun" is the Dawn Prayer, and "before its setting" is 'Asr, and the Prophet (ﷺ) explained it thus in the hadith agreed upon as authentic from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: (p-3963) 'Indeed you will see your Lord just as you see this moon on the night of the full moon, and if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and a prayer before its setting, then do so.' Then he recited His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130]." His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and during the night﴾ [al-Isra': 79], ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130], is unrestricted regarding the hours of the night, encompassing Maghrib and 'Isha'. Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, stated this in his fatwa on "the Great Prayer Times" (al-Mawaqit al-Kubra).

Third: This verse is among the verses in which Exalted is He commanded the establishment of the prayer at its time. Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his aforementioned fatwa: The time of the prayer has two kinds: the time of ease and choice, and the time of need and excuse. The time in a state of ease is five times, as in Sahih Muslim from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The time of Zuhr is as long as the shadow of a thing is not equal to it. The time of 'Asr is as long as the sun has not turned yellow. The time of Maghrib is as long as the twilight (shafaq) has not disappeared. The time of 'Isha' is until the middle of the night. The time of Fajr is as long as the sun has not risen." This hadith is also narrated from Abu Hurayrah in the Sunan. Nothing was related from the Prophet (ﷺ) about the times in his own words except this. Everything else that is related is about his deeds, and the authentic later reports of his deeds agree with this hadith. For this reason, what is in this hadith about the times is the sound view according to the jurists expert in hadith. The disagreement among the scholars concerns the end of the time of Zuhr, the beginning and end of the time of 'Asr, the end of the time of Maghrib, the end of the time of 'Isha', and the end of the time of Fajr. The majority of the early and later scholars, the jurists of hadith and the people of the Hijaz, hold that the time of Zuhr is from the declining until the shadow of every thing becomes equal to it, apart from the shade on which the sun declined. This is the school of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad. Abu Hanifah said: until the shadow of every thing becomes twice its length. Then the time of 'Asr enters according to the majority; but according to Abu Hanifah it enters only when the shadow of every thing becomes twice its length. It is reported from him that the period between one times its length and two times its length is neither the time of Zuhr nor the time of [p. 3964] 'Asr. According to the view of the majority, is the end of this the beginning of that, or is there between them a shared period of about four rak'ahs? There is disagreement about this. The majority hold the first, and the second is reported from Malik. When the shadow of every thing becomes twice its length, the time of 'Asr expires according to one of the two narrations from Ahmad. This is also reported from Malik and al-Shafi'i, with a disagreement in their schools. The correct view is that its time extends without disapproval until the sun becomes yellow. This is the second narration from Ahmad, as the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr states, which the Prophet (ﷺ) acted upon in Madinah after his practice in Makkah. This is the view of Abu Yusuf and Muhammad. Thus there was no agreed-upon time for 'Asr. But the correct and definitive view, which has been transmitted by continuous reports and agreed upon by the majority, is that its time enters when the shadow of every thing becomes equal to it. There is no report from the Prophet (ﷺ) supporting the other view, neither sound nor weak. However, the rulers who used to delay the prayer, when they became accustomed to delaying the prayer and this became well known, some people came to think that it was the Sunnah. It was argued in its favour by the parable struck for the Muslims and the People of the Book. But there is no proof in it, since there is agreement among the people of calculation that the time of Zuhr is longer than the time of 'Asr, whose beginning is when the shadow of every thing becomes twice its length.

The times of need and excuse are three: from midday (zawal) until sunset (ghurub); from sunset until dawn (fajr); and from dawn until sunrise. The first is the time of Zuhr and 'Asr in cases of excuse, and it is widened for them in two ways. One is advancing 'Asr to the time of Zuhr, as the Prophet (ﷺ) advanced it on the day of 'Arafah, and as he used to advance it on the expedition to Tabuk when he set out after the sun had declined. And advancing 'Isha to Maghrib in rain. This is jam' taqdim (combining by advancing). The second is jam' ta'khir (combining by delaying), in which 'Asr is delayed until sunset, based on the sound hadith in which the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever catches one rak'ah of Fajr before the sun rises has caught Fajr. And whoever catches one rak'ah of 'Asr before the sun sets has caught 'Asr." Together with his saying (ﷺ) in the sound hadith: "The time of 'Asr is as long as the sun has not turned yellow," and the fact that he never delayed the prayer until it turned yellow. The day of the Trench, the delay was until after sunset, and this was abrogated according to the more well-known of the two opinions of the scholars, by the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Guard the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 238]. This is the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad in the more well-known of his two reports. It is said that one may choose during fighting between delaying and praying within the time, according to what is possible. This is his other report. It is also said: rather, one delays it. This is also the view of Abu Hanifah. In the sound hadith from him (ﷺ) he said: "That is the prayer of the hypocrite, that is the prayer of the hypocrite, that is the prayer of the hypocrite, who watches the sun until it is between the two horns of the devil, then stands and pecks four times, remembering Allah in it only a little." So he described the prayer of the hypocrite by delaying it until the time of sunset and by pecking. This indicates prohibition of both this and that. When the Prophet (ﷺ) said both this and that, it is known that the time has two times. Whoever catches one rak'ah of 'Asr before the sun sets has caught it absolutely, but he is not permitted to delay until that time while it is possible to pray before it. This is unlike one for whom praying before that is not possible, such as a menstruating woman who becomes pure, a madman who regains consciousness, a sleeper who awakes, and a forgetful person who remembers. The advancing of 'Asr on the day of 'Arafah indicates that it is performed together with Zuhr immediately after zawal in one place. This hadith indicates that its time is attained by catching one rak'ah of it before sunset. Moreover, he clarified by his saying and his action that its time is when the shadow of everything becomes equal to it, as long as the sun has not turned yellow. This indicates that this time specific to it is a time of ease and comfort; no one may delay it beyond it or advance it before it. It is known from the Companions, such as 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, Abu Hurayrah, and Ibn 'Abbas, that they said (concerning a menstruating woman who becomes pure before sunset): she prays Zuhr and 'Asr. And if she becomes pure before dawn, she prays Maghrib and 'Isha. No dissent from any Companion is known. The majority took this view, such as Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad. This indicates that the Companions held that the night, in cases of excuse, is shared between Maghrib and 'Isha until dawn, and the second half, in cases of excuse, is shared between Zuhr and 'Asr from zawal until sunset. As the Sunnah and the Qur'an indicate, meaning the verse mentioned and similar verses we have cited before. Those who dispute with the majority about the shared time, and say that each of the two has only a time specific to it, say: the purpose was established by the Qur'an, and the Qur'an made the absolute remembrance obligatory in His saying: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies himself﴾ [al-A'la: 14] ﴿and remembers the name of his Lord and prays﴾ [al-A'la: 15]. So there is no requirement for specifically takbir in their view, but rather absolute remembrance. Although the Prophet (ﷺ) never prayed except with takbir, and none of his successors nor any of the imams of the Muslims nor any of their well-known individuals is known to have prayed except with takbir, yet they permit it with absolute remembrance, because the Qur'an is absolute in remembrance. It is said to them: the Qur'an is absolute regarding the hours of the night and the darkness of the night, and absolute regarding the first end and the second end, so this indicates permissibility of prayer in this and that, even if it were assumed that the Prophet (ﷺ) constantly separated them. How much more so when it is established from him that he combined them within the time more than once! Likewise they say: His saying, Exalted: ﴿Bow and prostrate﴾ [al-Hajj: 77] is absolute. It is the obligation, and tranquility (tuma'ninah) came only by a single report, which yields obligation but not fardiyyah (being a pillar). Likewise they say concerning al-Fatihah: the Qur'an is absolute in requiring the recitation of what is easy of it, although the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims after him prayed only with al-Fatihah. And with his saying: "There is no prayer except with Umm al-Qur'an" and "Every prayer in which Umm al-Qur'an is not recited is deficient (khidaj), deficient, deficient." They say: this indicates obligation but not fardiyyah. Or: this is a single report, so the absolute Qur'an is not restricted by it. It is known that the Qur'an is absolute regarding the shared time to a greater degree than this, and they have nothing from the Prophet (ﷺ) that requires performing each of the four in its specific time except his mutawatir action and his saying, which is among the single reports, along with its ambiguity, like his saying when he explained the five prescribed times: "The time is between these two," and his saying: "Between these two is a time." Its indication of the obligation of prayer in this time is not stronger than the indication of his saying: "There is no prayer except with Umm al-Kitab," and his saying: "Whoever prays a prayer in which he does not recite Umm al-Kitab, it is deficient." Likewise his saying (ﷺ) in the sound hadith: "After me there will be rulers who delay the prayer from its time, so pray the prayer at its time, then make your prayer with them a voluntary prayer." Hence Ahmad argued for the obligation of performing it within its time in ease, by his saying (ﷺ): "Pray the prayer at its time," which is the time he specified for them. The rulers did not delay the daytime prayer until night, nor the night prayer until day; rather they delayed Zuhr until the time of 'Asr and 'Asr until the end of the day. This indicates that whoever does this is not to be fought, for they asked him about the rulers: shall we fight them? He said: "No, as long as they pray." And this was their prayer. It indicates that this prayer is not permissible in any case, and that missing the day of the Trench is abrogated. As for combining the two in the shared time, it is established in the Sunnah in multiple places, and some of it is agreed upon by the Muslims. The well-known reports from the Companions show that the shared time is a time in a state of excuse, like the saying of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: "Combining between two prayers without an excuse is among the major sins," which indicates that combining them for an excuse is permissible. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, Ibn 'Abbas, and Abu Hurayrah said concerning one who became pure at the end of the day: she prays Zuhr and 'Asr; and concerning one who became pure at the end of the night: she prays Maghrib and 'Isha. This is the view of the three: Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad. As for missing the prayer, it is never permissible in any case. Whoever permits missing it in some cases, his view is weak, even if he permits combining. As for whoever requires missing it and prohibits combining, he has combined in his view two weak principles: permitting what Allah and His Messenger forbade, and forbidding what Allah and His Messenger prescribed. For it is established that combining is better than missing. This principle organizes many of the times. Missing 'Asr until the time of yellowing is not permitted, and missing 'Isha until the second half is also not permitted except out of necessity. Combining the two prayers is better than praying in that time; indeed praying with tayammum before the entry of the time of necessity is better than praying with wudu' in the time of necessity. The jurists among the followers of Ahmad and others have explicitly stated this, and they said: it is not permissible to delay it until yellowing. Rather, if he finds water only in that time, he prays with tayammum before yellowing, and does not pray it at the time of yellowing with wudu'. End of his words, may mercy be upon him.

And His saying, Exalted:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[79] ﴿And during part of the night, perform tahajjud (night prayer) with it, as a supererogatory act for you. It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station.﴾

﴿And during part of the night, perform tahajjud with it, as a supererogatory act for you﴾ is a command to him to pray at night, following His command to perform the five daily prayers. The word ﴿min﴾ ("during") has two possible functions. The first is that it is connected to ﴿tahajjud﴾, meaning: perform tahajjud with the Qur'an during part of the night. The second is that it is connected to an implied verb to which ﴿fatahajjad﴾ is conjoined, meaning: stand (for prayer) during part of the night, and so perform tahajjud with the Qur'an. Tahajjud (the act of rising from sleep to pray) is the removal of hujud, which is sleep, and the form tafa''ala can denote removal, as in ta'atham and tahara which mean "to abandon sin" and "to abandon wrongdoing." Al-Azhari said: "The well-known usage in the Arabic language is that the hajid is the one who sleeps, while the mutahajjid is the one who rises from sleep to pray. It is as if he is called mutahajjid because he has cast off sleep from himself, just as the worshipper is called mutahannith because he has cast off sinning (hinth) from himself." End of quotation.

It is related from Ibn Faris that its meaning is "pray at night," and similarly from Ibn al-A'rabi, who said: "hajada al-rajul and tahajjada" means when a man prays at night. The first meaning is the well-known one. The pronoun in ﴿bihi﴾ ("with it") refers to the Qur'an as such, not restricted by its being connected to the dawn, or it refers to the part of the night understood from ﴿min﴾, and the ba' is in the sense of fi ("during"), meaning: perform tahajjud during that part. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿nafilah laka﴾ ("a supererogatory act for you"), means an additional act of worship beyond the five prayers.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "He placed nafilah in the position of tahajjud, because tahajjud is an additional act of worship. So tahajjud and nafilah share one meaning. The meaning is that tahajjud was added for you beyond the obligatory prayers, as an obligation upon you alone and not others, because for them it is voluntary." End of quotation.

Abu al-Su'ud said: "Perhaps this is the reason it is mentioned after the mention of the dawn prayer, even though its time precedes it." 

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾ means: the one who stands in it will be praised, and everyone who sees him and knows him will praise him. It is general in covering everything that brings praise of the various kinds of honors. The well-known view is that it is the station of the great intercession (al-shafa'ah al-'uzma, the intercession for mankind), because of the judgment between the creatures, in which the first and last generations will praise him, as the authentic reports have related. The meaning of the noble verse according to this view is: just as you rose from sleep, which is the lesser death, through prayer and worship, He will raise you after the greater death, to a praised station in your sight and in the sight of all people. In this there is an easing of the hardship of standing in prayer at night. Abu al-Su'ud indicated this.

Note:
Ibn Jarir said: "Others held that this praised station, which Allah promised His Prophet (ﷺ) that He would raise him to, is that He will seat him with Him upon His Throne. This was related by Layth from Mujahid. Al-Wahidi censured the one who holds this view, although he himself also related it from Ibn Mas'ud. His words, as quoted by al-Razi, are: '(This is a base, repulsive and monstrous view, and the text of the Book calls out against the corruption of this interpretation and indicates it by several points:

The first: that al-ba'th (raising, sending forth) is the opposite of al-ij'las (causing to sit). It is said: "I raised the one standing and the one sitting, so he rose," and "Allah raised the dead," meaning He restored him from his grave. So interpreting al-ba'th as al-ij'las is interpreting the opposite by its opposite, which is invalid.

The second: that He, exalted is He, said ﴿a praised station (maqaman mahmudan)﴾ and did not say "a praised seat (maq'adan)." Al-maqam is the place of standing, not the place of sitting.

The third: if He, exalted is He, were sitting upon the Throne, such that Muhammad, peace be upon him, sat beside Him, then He would be bounded and finite. Whatever is so is originated.

The fourth: it is said that his sitting with Allah upon the Throne contains no great honor, because these ignorant and foolish people say (regarding all the people of Paradise) that they visit Allah, exalted is He, that they sit with Him, and that He, exalted is He, asks them about their conditions that they were in during the world. If this state is attained by all believers, there would be no additional distinction or rank in specifying Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with it.

The fifth: if it is said, "The sultan sent so-and-so," it is understood that he sent him to a people to resolve their affairs. It is not understood from this that he seated him with himself. Thus it is established that this view is a base, worthless statement, which no one inclines toward except a person of little intellect and no religion.)' End of the words of al-Wahidi."

I wish he had looked at what Ibn Jarir wrote, so that he would restrain the bridle of his pen and observe the courtesy due to the early scholars along with their scholarly reasoning. Here is what Ibn Jarir said, may Allah have mercy on him, after quoting Mujahid's statement mentioned above:

"The more correct of the two views is what the report has authenticated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that it is the station of intercession." Then he said: "And although this is the correct view regarding the interpretation of the praised station, because of the transmission we have mentioned from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his companions and the Successors, what Mujahid said, that Allah seats Muhammad (ﷺ) upon His Throne, is a statement whose soundness cannot be rejected, neither from the standpoint of report nor of reasoning. This is because there is no report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), nor from any of his companions, nor from the Successors, which rules it out. As for reasoning, all who profess Islam differ about the meaning of this in three ways. One group among them said: Allah, mighty and majestic, is separate from His creation. He existed before creating things, then He created things without touching them, and He is as He always was. However, the things He created, if He is not touching them, must be separate from them, since there is no act upon things except by one who either touches bodies or is separate from them. They said: If this is so, and Allah, mighty and majestic, is the Doer of things, and it is not permissible in their view to describe Him as touching things, then by their assumption He must be separate from them. So according to the doctrine of these people, it is the same whether Muhammad (ﷺ) is seated upon His Throne or upon the earth (since in their view His separation from His Throne and His separation from His earth are the same in meaning, in that He is separate from both of them and touches neither of them).

Another group said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, before creating things, had nothing touching Him and nothing separate from Him. Then He created things and established them by His power, and He is as He was before creating things, having nothing touching Him and nothing separate from Him. According to the view of these people as well: it is the same whether Muhammad (ﷺ) is seated upon His Throne or upon His earth (since in their view His Throne and His earth are the same, in that He touches neither of them and is separate from neither of them).

Another group said: Allah, mighty is His remembrance, before creating things, had nothing touching Him and nothing separate from Him. Then He originated things and created them, and He created for Himself a Throne upon which He sat, and He came to touch it, just as before creating things He had nothing that He provided sustenance to, nor anything He withheld that from. Then He created things and provided for this one and withheld from that one, gave to this one and withheld from that one. They said: Thus He was before creating things, having nothing touching Him or separate from Him. Then He created things and touched the Throne by sitting upon it, apart from the rest of His creation, so He touches whatever of His creation He wills and is separate from whatever He wills of it. According to the doctrine of these people as well, it is the same whether He seats Muhammad upon His Throne or seats him upon a pulpit of light, since in their view the sitting of the Lord upon His Throne is not a sitting that occupies the whole Throne, nor does seating Muhammad (ﷺ) impose upon Him the attribute of lordship, nor remove him from the attribute of servanthood to his Lord. Just as the separation of Muhammad (ﷺ) from things that are separate from him does not impose upon him the attribute of lordship, nor remove him from the attribute of servanthood to his Lord, because he is described as separate from it, just as Allah, mighty and majestic, is described, according to the statement of the one who holds this view, as separate from them, He is separate from him. They said: If the meaning of 'separate' and 'separate' does not impose upon Muhammad (ﷺ) the departure from the attribute of servanthood and entry into the meaning of lordship, then likewise his sitting upon the Throne of the Merciful does not impose that upon him. Thus it has become clear from what we have said that it is not impossible, according to anyone among those who profess Islam, that what Mujahid said is true, that Allah, blessed and exalted, seats Muhammad upon His Throne. If someone says: We do not deny that Allah seats Muhammad upon His Throne, but we deny that He seats him with Him. (He narrated to me) Abbas ibn Abd al-'Azim, who said: Yahya ibn Kathir narrated to us from al-Jariri, from Sayf al-Sadusi, from Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: 'Muhammad (ﷺ) on the Day of Resurrection will be upon the Kursi (Footstool) of the Lord, before the Lord, blessed and exalted is He.' It is only his seating him with Him that they deny. It may be said: Is it permissible in your view that He seats him upon it and not with Him? If he permits that, he is compelled to acknowledge that either He is with him, or that He seats him, while Allah is separate from the Throne, or touches neither it nor is separate from it, and whichever of these he says, he has entered into some of what he was denying. If he says that this is not permissible for Him, he has departed from the view of all the sects we have related their views, and that is a separation from the view of all who profess Islam, since there is no view on this except those three views we have related. And among them, what Mujahid said is not impossible." End of the words of Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him.

I say: You may also answer the five objections of al-Wahidi, by which he corrupted Mujahid's view. As for his first objection, Mujahid did not interpret the root al-ba'th alone as al-ij'las. Rather, he interpreted His raising (ba'thahu) to the praised station with what he mentioned.

As for the second: al-maqam is the rank, the power and the elevation, and this is well known in the language.

As for the third: the stated consequence is rejected, because just as it is agreed that He has an essence unlike any other essences, likewise everything described of Him that has come in the Book and the reports does not resemble the attributes of creatures, and it is not permissible to analogize the Creator to the created.

As for the fourth: it is obstinacy, since everyone knows in the observable world that if a king summoned a group to attend before him, and raised the best of them upon his throne, the one raised is one of rank who surpasses all of them by it.

As for the fifth: it belongs to a different category from what we are discussing, since there is no sending forth to resolve matters in the Hereafter. The meaning of the verse is only: He will elevate you to a praised station. This agrees with what Mujahid said and what the majority said. So reflect and be fair.

The hafiz al-Dhahabi, in his book "Al-'Uluww li-Llah al-'Azim" (The Exaltation of Allah the Mighty), quoted in the biography of the Imam al-Daraqutni, the following verses:

Hadith of intercession concerning Ahmad, we ascribe it to Ahmad al-Mustafa (the Chosen).
As for the hadith of His seating him upon the Throne as well, we do not deny it.
Let the hadith pass as it stands, and do not introduce into it what corrupts it.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 17, verse 79 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Dhahabi said in his book *al-Munawwih bihi*, in the biography of Muhammad ibn Mus'ab, the worshipper, shaykh of Baghdad, the following: Al-Marwadhi said: I heard Abu 'Abdullah al-Khaffaf say: I heard Ibn Mus'ab recite: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾, and he said: Yes, He seats him upon the Throne. Imam Ahmad mentioned Muhammad ibn Mus'ab and said: I have written from him. And what kind of man is he?!

Al-Dhahabi said: As for the matter of our Prophet's sitting upon the Throne, no text has been established regarding it. Rather, on this topic there is only a weak (wahi) hadith. As for what Mujahid explained the verse by, as we have mentioned, some of the theologians (Ahl al-Kalam, the speculative theologians) have denied it. Al-Marwadhi then stood up, having gone to great lengths in defending it, and compiled a book on it, and traced the transmission of Mujahid's statement through the narrations of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, Abu Yahya al-Qattat and Jabir ibn Yazid. Among those who issued a legal opinion in that era, holding that this report is sound and is not to be opposed, were Abu Dawud al-Sijistani, author of the Sunan, Ibrahim al-Harbi, and a multitude. So much so that the son of Imam Ahmad said immediately after Mujahid's statement: I denounce everyone who rejects this hadith. And he is, in my view, an evil man, accused (of lying). I heard it from a group (of scholars). I have not seen any traditionist deny it. Among us, only the Jahmiyya (a heretical sect denying divine attributes) deny it. Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾ (p-٣٩٧٤) he said: He seats him upon the Throne. I related this to my father, may Allah have mercy on him, and he said: I was not destined to hear it from Ibn Fudayl.

So much so that al-Marwadhi related an account with the wording "descent," from Ibrahim ibn 'Arafa. And I heard Ibn 'Umayr say: I heard Ahmad ibn Hanbal say: The scholars have received this with acceptance. Al-Marwadhi said: Abu Dawud al-Sijistani said: Ibn Abi Safwan al-Thaqafi related to us, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to us, Salm ibn Ja'far related to us, and he was trustworthy, al-Jurayri related to us, Sayf al-Sadusi related to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, your Prophet (ﷺ) will be brought until he sits between the hands of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon His Kursi. (And so on, the hadith.)

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated it in his Tafsir, (namely the statement of Mujahid). Likewise al-Naqqash included it in his Tafsir. Likewise Ibn Surayj, shaykh of the Shafi'is, refuted those who denied it. So much so that Imam Abu Bakr al-Khallal said in his book *al-Sunna* from his compilation: al-Hasan ibn Salih al-'Attar informed me, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Sarraj, who said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) in a dream and I said: Indeed so-and-so al-Tirmidhi says: Allah does not seat you with Him upon the Throne. We say: Rather He does seat you. He turned to me, almost angry, and said: Yes, by Allah! Yes, by Allah! He seats me upon the Throne. Then I woke up.

So much so that the jurist Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Sulayman al-Najjad, the traditionist, said (as transmitted from him by the Qadi Abu Ya'la al-Farra'): If a swearer were to swear by divorce three times that Allah seats Muhammad (ﷺ) upon the Throne, and he asked me for a fatwa, I would tell him: You have spoken truly and you have been dutiful.

Al-Dhahabi said: Consider this, may Allah protect you from desire, how excess (ghuluw) led this traditionist to the obligation of acting upon an unreliable report. Today they reject the explicit hadiths about (Allah's) elevation. Rather, some of the riffraff try to reject His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5]. End.

And His saying, Exalted is He:
(p-٣٩٧٥)

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 17, verses 80–81:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[80-81] ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."﴾ ﴿And say, "The truth has come, and falsehood has departed. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart."﴾ [al-Isra: 81].

﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance"﴾ meaning: an entrance that is good and pleasing, free of blemish. ﴿And cause me to exit a sound exit﴾ meaning: an exit that is good and pleasing, free of the blemish of inclining toward the self, and free of straying after guidance. And ﴿grant me from Yourself a supporting authority﴾ meaning: a mighty power supporting Islam against disbelief, making it manifest over it.

Al-Mahayimi (al-Mahayimi) saw the connection of the verse with what precedes it in meaning, when he said: ﴿My Lord, cause me to enter﴾ meaning: into these acts of worship, for they will not bring you to the praiseworthy station unless your entering into them and your exiting from them is sincere, and this is not accomplished except by God's support after you seek help from Him. And your saying: ﴿My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance﴾ meaning: with Your witnessing in these acts of worship, and my being cleansed of ostentation and self-admiration, and my purification through sincerity of deed and sincerity in seeking the reward, and seeing the favor to God, and seeing my shortcoming in them. ﴿And cause me to exit﴾ from them ﴿a sound exit﴾, so do not employ me in what would nullify them for me, and do not return me to myself. And if Satan, or the self, or people overcome me, or a doubt comes upon me, then grant me from Yourself, not from my own reasoning, ﴿authority﴾ meaning: proof; ﴿supporting﴾ meaning: supporting me against what has been mentioned, so that He preserves my worship for me and brings me to the praiseworthy station. End quote.

The noble wording admits of this. And it appears to us that it is an allusion to the emigration (hijra), as you will see.

﴿And say﴾ [al-Isra: 81], meaning: rejoicing in the nearness of victory and triumph, and as a warning to the polytheists: ﴿The truth has come﴾ [al-Isra: 81], which is the promise of a supporting authority, and Islam and its dominion; ﴿and falsehood has departed﴾ [al-Isra: 81], meaning: went away and perished, which is polytheism and its rounds. ﴿Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart﴾ [al-Isra: 81], meaning: dissolving, not firm at any time.

(p-3976) Note:

The context of these verses together with what precedes them, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, they almost succeeded in driving you out of the land﴾ [al-Isra: 76], indicates that their revelation was at times of concern about the emigration to Madinah and departing from Makkah, and that He, exalted is He, commanded His Prophet to beseech Him to facilitate his entering with his emigrants in a manner that pleases Him, and his exit from his city likewise, and to grant him a protection from Himself that strengthens his side and保护s him from whoever intends him harm.

The method of the Mighty Revelation in such supplication is that the speaker expresses the report of the thing requested as already occurring, and that God wills its occurrence soon. For this reason He followed it with His saying: ﴿And say, "The truth has come, and falsehood has departed"﴾ [al-Isra: 81], informing that the matter is accomplished, the relief has come, falsehood has been repelled, and it has returned to its origin, which is nonexistence.

Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz narrated from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We entered Makkah with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols worshipped besides Allah. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded concerning them, and they were overturned upon their faces. And he said: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has departed; indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart﴾ [al-Isra: 81]." It was narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others from Ibn Mas'ud, similarly.

In al-Iklil, it said: In it is the recommendation of reciting this verse when removing an evil.
