Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 17, verse 82:

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained the loss of the polytheists through their turning away from that which cures their spiritual ailments, namely the Noble Qur'an, and the success of the believers through seeking healing by its guidance and mercy, in His saying:

**The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:**

[82] ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers; and it increases the wrongdoers in nothing but loss.﴾

﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers; and it increases the wrongdoers in nothing but loss.﴾ That is: And We send down to you of the Qur'an that by which one seeks healing from ignorance and misguidance. And a mercy, through the clarification of realities and the establishment of proofs, for those who believe in it, but not for the disbelievers. This is because the believers act upon what it contains of the obligations of Allah [p. 3977] and His laws. Thus He admits them into Paradise and saves them from punishment. So it is for them a mercy and a blessing. And it does not increase the wrongdoers, through their disbelief and polytheism, except in loss. That is: in ruin. For whenever a command or a prohibition from Allah comes to them, they disbelieve in it, and so it increases them in loss, in addition to what they were already in before, and in filth added to their filth.

Al-Shihab (al-Khafaji) said: "Ash-shifa'" (healing) is an explicit metaphor (isti'ara tasrihiyya) or an implicative metaphor (isti'ara takhyiliyya), by likening disbelief to sickness. And "min" (from) is explanatory (bayaniyya), placed before what it explains, which is "ma" (that which), for the sake of emphasis.

**Note:**

Some scholars held that the Qur'an is among the things by which physical ailments are cured, on the basis of this verse, by taking the word "shifa'" in two meanings, through the category of the generality of metaphor (umum al-majaz), or by taking the homonym (mushtarak) in both of its meanings. Among those who affirmed this is al-Razi (Fakhr al-Din al-Razi). His words are: Know that the Qur'an is a healing from spiritual ailments, and also a healing from bodily ailments. As for its being a healing from spiritual ailments, it is evident. This is because spiritual ailments are of two kinds: false beliefs and blameworthy character traits. As for false beliefs, the most severe of them is corruption of belief concerning the divine matters, prophethood, the afterlife, and destiny and predestination (al-qada' wa al-qadar). The Qur'an contains proofs for the correct doctrine on these matters and the refutation of false doctrines concerning them. Therefore, it is undoubtedly a healing from this type of spiritual sickness. As for blameworthy character traits, the Qur'an contains a detailed explanation of them, a definition of the corruptions they contain, and guidance towards virtuous and perfect character traits and praiseworthy deeds. Thus the Qur'an is a healing from this type of sickness. So it is established that the Qur'an is a healing from all spiritual ailments.

As for its being a healing from bodily ailments, this is because seeking blessing through its recitation repels many illnesses. Since the majority of philosophers and the practitioners of talismans (al-tilasimat) have acknowledged that incantations (al-ruqa al-majhula) and formulas (al-'aza'im) whose meaning is not understood have great effects in bringing about benefits and repelling harms, then it is more fitting that the recitation of this great Qur'an, which contains the mention of Allah's majesty and greatness, the glorification of the angels brought near, and the belittling of the rebellious devils, should be a cause for obtaining benefit in religion and in the world. What we have mentioned is reinforced by the hadith: "Whoever does not seek healing by the Qur'an, may Allah not heal him." [p. 3978] As for its being a mercy for the believers, know that we have explained that human spirits are diseased because of false beliefs and corrupt character. The Qur'an includes that which grants deliverance from the doubts of the misguided and the deceptions of the falsifiers, and this is the healing. It also includes that which teaches how to acquire lofty sciences and virtuous character, by which a person reaches the presence of the Lord of the worlds and joins the company of the angels brought near; and this is the mercy. Since removing sickness precedes striving to complete the causes of health, Allah, exalted is He, in this verse began with mention of the healing and then followed it with mention of the mercy. End of quotation.

Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in Zad al-Ma'ad, in the section on simple medicines and foods which came from the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ), under the letter qaf (Qur'an): Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾. The correct view is that "min" here is for specifying the kind, not for partitioning. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts﴾ [Yunus: 57]. So the Qur'an is the complete healing from all diseases of the heart and body, and from the ailments of this world and the Hereafter. Not everyone is qualified for it, nor is everyone granted success in seeking healing by it. When the patient uses it well, applying it to his illness with sincerity, faith, complete acceptance, firm conviction, and fulfilling its conditions, the illness will never overcome it. How could illnesses overcome the speech of the Lord of the earth and heaven, which if it were sent down upon the mountains would split them, or upon the earth would cut it apart?! There is no illness of the hearts or bodies except that in the Qur'an there is a way to indicate its remedy, its cause, and the protection from it, for whoever Allah grants understanding of His Book. So whoever is not healed by the Qur'an, may Allah not heal him. And whoever is not sufficed by it, may Allah not suffice him.

Then he said under the letter kaf: A group of the early generations (al-salaf) permitted writing some of the Qur'an and drinking it, and this was considered part of the healing which Allah placed in it. Then he mentioned what Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya used to write for nosebleeds. Refer to it.

[p. 3979] It was mentioned earlier, in the beginning of the book, regarding the secret of its being a healing, that there are wondrous truths. And likewise in the section on incantation. It was also mentioned that among the remedies which heal illnesses are those which the minds of the great physicians have not reached, and which their knowledge, experiments, and analogies have not attained: the remedies of the heart and spirit, the strength of the heart and its reliance upon Allah, trust in Him, turning to Him, prostration and humbling before Him, submission to Him, charity, prayer, supplication, repentance, seeking forgiveness, kindness to creation, aiding the distressed, and relieving the afflicted. These remedies have been tested by nations of differing religions and creeds, and they found in them an effect on healing that the knowledge of the most knowledgeable physicians has not reached, nor its experience nor its analogy. We ourselves and others have tested many such things, and we have seen them accomplish what physical remedies do not accomplish. This runs according to the law of divine wisdom and is not outside of it. But the causes are varied, for when the heart is connected to the Lord of the worlds, the Creator of illness and cure, and the Manager of nature who directs it as He wills, it has other remedies besides the remedies that the heart distant from Him and turning away from Him uses. It is known that when spirits grow strong and the soul and nature grow strong, they cooperate in repelling illness and overcoming it. So how can it be denied that for one whose nature and soul are strong, and who rejoices in his nearness to his Creator, his intimacy with Him, his love for Him, his delight in remembering Him, the directing of all his powers toward Him, gathering them upon Him, seeking help from Him, and trusting in Him, this should be among the greatest remedies, and that this strength should cause the complete removal of pain?! Only the most ignorant of people, the most veiled, the densest of souls, and the furthest from Allah and from the reality of humanity would deny this.

And he, may God have mercy on him, has also elaborated in the book Ighathat al-Lahfan on the explanation of the Qur'an containing the remedies of the heart and its treatment from all its ailments, which is worth reviewing so that the seeker may increase in knowledge.

And His saying, exalted is He:

[p. 3980]

The discussion of the words of God Most High:

[83] ﴿And when We bestow favour upon man, he turns away and distances himself by his side; and when harm touches him, he is ever despairing.﴾

﴿And when We bestow favour upon man, he turns away and distances himself by his side; and when harm touches him, he is ever despairing.﴾ This is an indication of the cause of these misguided people falling into the valleys of error. It is the love of this world and preferring it over the Hereafter, and ingratitude for His blessings, Exalted is He, by turning away from giving thanks for them, and by anxiety and despair of relief when a harm that He has decreed befalls him. All of this is incompatible with the bond of faith. The believer looks with the eye of insight and witnesses the power of Allah Most High in both states. He is certain in the first state that gratitude is the tether of blessings, and in the second that patience is the defence against afflictions. So he gives thanks and he endures patiently. He knows that the Bestower is capable, so he does not turn away out of arrogance and insolence at the time of blessing, nor does he forget the Bestower, and he does not panic and fret at the time of affliction.

The verse is a description of the species by way of some of its individuals who are of this attribute, like His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us, then withdraw it from him, indeed he is despairing and ungrateful﴾ [Hud: 9] ﴿And if We let him taste favour after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "The evils have gone from me." Indeed, he is exultant and boastful﴾ [Hud: 10] ﴿Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [Hud: 11].

Al-Zamakhshari said: ﴿and distances himself by his side﴾ is an emphasis on turning away, because turning away from a thing is to turn the side of one's face away from it. Distancing by the side is to twist one's flank away from it and turn one's back to it. Or it is intended to mean arrogance, since that is the custom of the arrogant.

And His words, Exalted is He:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[84] ﴿Say: "Each acts according to his own manner (shakilah), but your Lord knows best who is best guided in the way."﴾

﴿Say: Each acts according to his own manner (shakilah)﴾ — that is: according to his own way (madhhab), his path (tariqah), his disposition (khaliqah), and his dominant faculty (malakah) which prevails over him, which arises in him from the predisposition of his true nature, and which corresponds to his state in guidance and error. It is from the phrase of the Arabs, "a path with many shawakil," meaning the roads that branch off from it because of their resemblance to one another, i.e., their similarity in form. The man's habit is named after this because it corresponds to his state. The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿but your Lord knows best who is best guided in the way﴾ — that is, who has the firmer (asadd) way (madhhab) and path (tariqah), of the two doers: the doer of good according to the requirement of the excellent disposition of the heart, and the doer of evil according to the requirement of the nature of the soul. So He will recompense each of them according to their deeds.

And His saying, exalted is He:

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 17, verse 85 (part 1 of 3)**

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[85] ﴿They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord, and you have been given only a little knowledge.﴾

﴿They ask you about the soul.﴾ Al-Qashani said: That is, the thing by which the human body lives and which governs it. ﴿Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord.﴾ That is, it is not from the world of creation, so that it could be made known to the outward, bodily people, whose perception goes beyond sense and the sensed, by way of comparison with some of what they have perceived and by description. Rather, it is from the world of command, that is, the world of origination, which is the world of essences stripped of matter, and of substances sanctified above form, color, direction and place. Therefore you cannot perceive it, O you who are veiled by created existence, because your perception and knowledge fall short of it. ﴿And you have been given only a little knowledge﴾ means the knowledge of sensible things. That is a paltry, insignificant thing compared with the knowledge of God and of those firmly rooted in knowledge. This is what al-Qashani said. The gist of the reply to him is that the soul is a created existence brought into being by His command, may He be exalted, without matter, and it is not generated from a source like the organs of the body, (p-3982) so that it could be made known through some of its principles. Rather, it is from the world of command, not from the world of creation. Thus the answer is limited to His words: ﴿The soul is by the command of my Lord,﴾ just as Moses, in answer to Pharaoh's words: ﴿And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 23], limited himself to: ﴿The Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 24], to inform him that grasping its essence as it truly is belongs to God alone, may He be exalted; and that it is a thing by whose departure a person dies, and by whose staying with him he remains alive. This is what His words, may He be exalted, hint at: ﴿And you have been given only a little knowledge,﴾ that is, a little knowledge that you acquire through the channels of the senses. And this is that general measure.

Al-Shihab said: The question, on this reading, concerns its reality, and the answer is a general one: that it is among the originated things without matter. For this reason it has been said that it is of the wise mode of address, as in His words: ﴿They ask you about the crescent moons﴾ [al-Baqarah: 189], indicating that its reality is not known, and that only this much of it is known from it. So the meaning of "command" on this interpretation is the saying "Be" (kun). For this reason they said of its like: "the knower of the command." End of quotation.

Abu al-Su'ud, may mercy be upon him, said: This is not of the kind of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only to say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya Sin: 82], for that is an expression of the swiftness of bringing into being, whether the thing that comes to be is of the world of command or of the world of creation. Rather, it is among the originated things that come to be by the sheer command of bringing into being, without being formed from matter. He, may mercy be upon him, also related another opinion, which is that "command" means "affair" (sha'n). He said: The attribution here is for knowledge-specificity, not for origination, since all share in it. And in it is an honoring of the thing attributed, which is not hidden. As in the second attribution, there is an honoring of the thing attributed to. That is: it is of the kind of the secrets hidden in God's knowledge, about which the minds of men scarcely hover. On this reading, "from" (min) is explanatory or partitive. It would be a prohibition for them from asking about it, and a leaving aside of explanation. This is the view of many, who refrained from delving into it and said: It is a thing whose knowledge God has kept to Himself and has not disclosed to any of His creatures. So it is not permissible to investigate it beyond saying that it is an existing thing. Some even went to extremes and said: Going deeply into the discussion of the soul is an innovation (bid'ah) in religion, if God has not explained it to His Messenger beyond what is in the verse. So occupying oneself with searching for it is excess concerning what no Qur'an has come with and no proof has established. Whatever is like this is obstinacy.

Those who delved into the investigation of it replied that the meaning of the verse does not indicate a definitive proof, nor is there in it any evidence forbidding delving into it, nor evidence that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not know it. The most that can be said is that he was commanded to leave off answering about it in detail. Either because refraining from that was among the signs of his prophethood for the Jewish questioners about it, or because their question was a provocation. For it is applied to several meanings: among them rest, the coolness of the breeze, Gabriel, the Qur'an, Jesus, peace be upon him, life, the heart, mercy, and other things. They secretly intended that if he answered with one of these matters, they would say: "We did not mean that; we meant such-and-such."

Then the sayings about it among the ancient sages and scholars differ, and the answer cannot be complete on the point of disagreement. So he gave the answer in general terms, in a way that would be confirmed for each of these meanings in a coded manner, so that the scholars of God would understand it. And the general welfare required prohibiting speech about it for others, because minds cannot bear it, especially according to the method of the sages. For whoever has a nature dominated by rigidity does not accept it, nor believe in it concerning the attributes of the Creator; so how would he believe in it concerning the human soul? Indeed, some careful scholars said: In the verse and the answer there is an explanation of its reality, that it is among His originated things that come to be by His bringing into being, without any prior matter. This is what we mentioned first. In answering with this there is sufficiency for people of insight and understanding, and it is persuasive for whoever has a hope of settling the dispute if it is explained in detail. Some of them approved this answer and, appending to it, said: Then His words, ﴿Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord,﴾ on the reading that the question concerns its reality, correspond to it, except that the answer is general, meaning: it is among the things possible to grasp, whose realities can be reached through the exercise of reflection and the awakening of thought, like the rest of the world of command. And on the reading that the question concerns its eternity and its being originated, it is likewise, except that the answer is detailed. In any case, He did not leave (p-3984) its explanation aside. And if it were among things for which there is no way to know, it would have been said: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾ [al-A'raf: 187], as was said about the Hour, or something similar. Indeed, if there were no path to knowing it, even in some way, accessible to many people, then His command to reflect upon it and to contemplate its matter, in order to derive proof of Him from it and to reach Him through knowledge of it, which is the supreme goal and the greatest fruit, would have no benefit; rather it would be pointless. So His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they not reflect within themselves?﴾ [al-Rum: 8], and His words: ﴿And within yourselves; will you not see?﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 21], and similar verses, indicate that it is a matter the intellects can perceive, and through it the arrival at Him, may He be exalted, is achieved.

Then, the reports of those who delved into the investigation of it are varied. Old and modern works have been devoted to that, and what concerns us is knowing what the careful imams relied upon, those who sifted through the sayings of earlier scholars and tested them against the touchstone of the Book and the Sunnah, rejecting what contradicts them and adhering to what agrees with them.

Among them is the Imam Ibn Hazm. He said, may God have mercy on him, in his book (al-Milal wa al-Nihal), after listing various doctrines: The whole of the people of Islam and the religions that affirm the Return have held that the soul is a long, broad, deep body, possessing place, rational, discerning, directing the body. He said: And this is what we say. The soul and the spirit are two names for one named thing, and their meaning is one. Then he said: As for one who holds that the soul is not a body, that view is refuted by the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the consensus (ijma') of the Community. As for the Qur'an, God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿There every soul will experience what it sent forth before﴾ [Yunus: 30]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned; no injustice today﴾ [Ghafir: 17]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he earned﴾ [al-Tur: 21]. Thus it is established that the soul is the one that acts, earns, responds and errs. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the soul commands to evil﴾ [Yusuf: 53]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established: admit the people of Pharaoh to the severest punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 46]. He, may He be exalted, said: (p-3985) ﴿And do not say of those killed in the way of God, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive﴾ [al-Baqarah: 154]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And do not think of those killed in the way of God as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, provided for﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169], ﴿rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty﴾ [Al 'Imran: 170]. Thus it is established that some souls are presented to the Fire before the Day of Resurrection and are punished; and some are provided for and made to enjoy, rejoicing, and are joyful before the Resurrection. There is no doubt that the bodies of the people of Pharaoh and the bodies of those killed in the way of God have had their limbs torn apart, and have been eaten by beasts, birds and sea creatures. Thus it is established that souls are transferred from place to place. And there is no doubt that an accident does not receive punishment nor feel, so the soul is not an accident. And it is established that it moves about in places existing by itself, and this is the attribute of a body, not the attribute of a substance according to the one who holds it. Therefore it is established, necessarily, that it is a body.

As for the Sunnah, there is the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "The souls of martyrs are in the crops of green birds in Paradise." And his saying (ﷺ) that he "saw the spirits (nisam) of the children of Adam at the lowest heaven, on the right and left of Adam." Thus it is established that souls are seen in their places. And his saying, peace be upon him: "When the soul of the believer is taken, it is raised up to heaven and such-and-such is done to it; and when the soul of the disbeliever is taken, such-and-such is done to it." Thus it is established that they are punished, made to enjoy, and transferred from place to place, and this is necessarily the attribute of bodies.

As for the consensus, there is no disagreement among anyone of the people of Islam that the souls of the servants, after their departure from the bodies, are transferred to bliss or to various kinds of distress and punishment. And this is the attribute of bodies.

Then he said: The meaning of God's words, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord,﴾ (p-3986) is only that the body is created from dust, then from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, then bones, then flesh, then mixed substances. The soul is not like that. Rather, God, may He be exalted, commanding it to exist, said "Be," and it was. Thus it is established that the soul, the spirit and the breath are synonymous names for one meaning. The word "spirit" is also used for other things besides this. Gabriel, peace be upon him, is "the Trustworthy Spirit." And the Qur'an is "a spirit from God."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 17, verse 85 (part 2 of 3):

Ibn Hazm also said, before that, in the discussion of the punishment of the grave: "What we hold concerning the abode of the souls (*mustaqarr al-arwah*) is what Allah the Exalted and His Prophet (ﷺ) said, and we do not go beyond it. The clear proof is that Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify." [This] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this."﴾ [al-A'raf: 172]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We have certainly created you, then formed you, then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated﴾ [al-A'raf: 11]. So it is established that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the souls (*al-arwah*) collectively, and they are the selves (*al-anfus*). Likewise, he (peace be upon him) informed: "The souls are armies mobilized; whatever among them becomes acquainted, unites, and whatever among them is unfamiliar, differs." They are the rational and perceptive [entities], and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took their covenant and their testimony. They are created, formed, and rational before He commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, may peace be upon all of them, and before He caused them to enter the bodies. At that time, the bodies were dust and water. Then the Exalted placed them wherever He willed, because Allah the Exalted mentioned that using the particle (*thumma*, "then"), which indicates sequence and an interval. Then Mighty and Majestic He placed them wherever He willed, and this is the barzakh to which they return at death. He continuously sends forth from them one group after another, and He breathes them into the bodies that are formed from the semen that flows from the loins of men and the wombs of women, as the Exalted said: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted [in a womb]?﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 37] ﴿Then he became a clinging clot, and He created [him] and proportioned [him]﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 38].

(p. 3987) And Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And We did certainly create man from an extract of clay﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12] ﴿Then We made him a drop [of sperm] in a secure place﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 13] ﴿Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a lump, then We made the lump into bones﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14], to the end of the verse. Likewise the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed: "The creation of the son of Adam is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days as a drop, then similarly as a clot, then similarly as a lump, then an angel is sent to him and he breathes the soul into him." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, tests them in this world as He wills. Then He takes them back (*yatawaffa-ha*), and they return to the barzakh in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw them on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), at the lowest heaven: the souls of the people of happiness are on the right of Adam, peace be upon him, and the souls of the people of misery are on his left, peace be upon him. This is at the cessation of the elements (*mun-qata' al-'anasir*), and the souls of the prophets, peace be upon them, and the souls of the martyrs are hastened to Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi related from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh that he mentioned this very view which we have stated, and said: "Upon this the people of knowledge (*ahl al-'ilm*) have agreed (*ajma'*)."

Then Ibn Hazm said: "The souls remain there until Allah completes the number of all the souls by breathing them into their bodies, then by their return to the aforementioned barzakh. Then the Hour will come, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will return the souls a second time to the bodies. This is the second life. He will call the creation to account: a group will be in Paradise and a group in the blazing Fire, abiding forever." End of quotation.

**Section**

Among them is Shaykh al-Islam Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, who said in *Tafsir Surat al-Ikhlas* (*Tafsir Surah al-Ikhlas*), after mentioning the dispute of the theologians (*al-mutakallimun*, the scholastic theologians) and the philosophers (*al-mutafalsifah*) concerning the angels: Are they located in space or not? Likewise is their dispute concerning the spirit of the human being which departs from him at death, according to the view of the majority (*al-jumhur*) who say: it is a self-subsisting entity (*'ayn qa'imah bi-nafsiha*), not an accident (*'arad*) of the body such as life and others, nor a part of the parts of the body such as the air that exits from it. For many of the theologians claimed that it is an accident subsisting in the body, or a part of the parts of the body. But this contradicts the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus (*ijma'*, scholarly agreement) of the early and later generations (*al-salaf wa-al-khalaf*), and the view of the majority of intelligent people from all nations. It also contradicts the evidences. This is one of the things with which the philosophers prevailed over many of the people of kalam (*ahl al-kalam*, dialectical theology).

Qadi Abu Bakr [al-Baqillani] said: "Most of the theologians hold that the spirit is an accident among the accidents. We also say this, if by 'spirit' one does not mean the self (*nafs*). For he said: The spirit that is in the body has two kinds: one is the life subsisting in it, and the other is the self. The self is a wind that spreads through it, and what is meant by the self is what comes out with the breath from the particles of air dispersed through the pores." This is the view of al-Isfara'ini and others. Ibn Furak said: "It is what flows in the cavities of the organs." Abu al-Ma'ali (al-Juwayni) differed from these and did well in differing, saying: "The spirit is subtle bodies intertwined with the perceptible bodies. Allah has established the custom that the bodies live as long as their intertwining with them continues. When they depart from them, death follows life according to the continuing custom."

The doctrine of the Companions and of the Successors who followed them in excellence, and of the rest of the early community (*salaf al-ummah*) and the imams of the Sunnah, is that the spirit is a self-subsisting entity. It departs from the body, and it is given bliss and punished. It is not the body, nor a part of its parts, like the self mentioned above.

Then those who said it is an entity disputed: is it a located body (*jism mutahayyiz*)? There are two views, like their dispute concerning the angels. The theologians among them say: it is a body. The philosophers say: it is a rational substance (*jawhar 'aqli*) that is not a body. The origin of their naming of the separated and detached entities (*al-mujarradat wa-al-mufariqat*) is derived from the very self of the human being. For since it departs from his body at death and becomes detached from it, they named it "separated and detached." Then they established what they established of intellects and souls and named them "separated and detached," because they are separated from matter, which for them is the body. These separated entities, according to them, are neither bodies nor subsisting in bodies. But the self is attached to the body in the manner of governing (*ta'alluq al-tadbir*), while the intellect has no attachment to bodies at all. There is no doubt that the majority of intelligent people agree on establishing a difference between the body and the spirit, which departs.

(p. 3989) The majority call that a spirit, and this a body. But the word "body" (*jism*) in the language is not the same as "body" in the terminology of the theologians. Rather, *jism* is the body (*jasad*), which is the coarse body, or its coarseness. The spirit is not like the body in coarseness and density, and for this reason it is not called a *jism*. So whoever makes the angels and spirits a body in the linguistic sense has not erred in that. As for the people of the technical terminology among the theologians and the philosophers, they make the referent of "body" more general than that: it is what can be indicated by sensory pointing, and what is said to be "here" or "there," and what is before the three dimensions, and similar things.

Then he (may Allah have mercy on him) said: What these philosophers say about the rational soul, that it cannot be pointed to, cannot be described with motion, rest, ascent, or descent, and is neither inside the world nor outside it, is a false statement according to the majority of intelligent people. Especially one who says, like Ibn Sina and his like, that it does not know any of the particular matters but only knows universal matters. For this is manifest arrogance, since it knows its body, knows everything it sees with the body, smells, hears, tastes, intends, commands, loves, and dislikes, and other things in which it acts through its knowledge and its work. So how can it be said that it does not know specific matters, and knows only universal matters?! Likewise their saying that its attachment to the body is nothing but the mere attachment of governing and directing, like the king's governing of his kingdom, is among the most corrupt speech. For the king governs the affairs of his kingdom, commanding and forbidding, but he does not move them by his will and power if they do not move by their own will and power. The king does not feel the pleasure of any one of them, nor the pain of their pain, whereas that is not the case with the spirit and the body. Rather, Allah has placed between them a union and harmony for which no comparable analogy is known. But the entry of the spirit into it is not like the entry of any of the perceptible bodies. Its entry is not like the entry of water and similar liquids into vessels, for these only touch the inner surface of the vessels, not their bottoms or their backs, and only their edges touch the vessels, not their middles. But the spirit and the body are not so: the spirit (p. 3990) is attached to all the parts of the body, inner and outer. Likewise its entry into it is not like the entry of food and drink into the body of the one who eats, for that has known channels and is transformed into other attributes. Nor is its flowing in the body like the flowing of blood, for blood is in some parts of the body and not others. In sum, none of the analogies that are mentioned is such that each thing in it is attached to the other, unlike the spirit and the body. Yet despite this, it has entered the body, and it exits from it at the time of death, and is drawn out from it little by little. It leaves the body little by little. It does not depart from it as the king departs from the city he governs. Since people have not witnessed any analogue for it, it is difficult for them to express its reality. This is a reminder to them of the Lord of the worlds, since they have not known His reality, nor conceived how He is, glory be to Him and exalted. What is attributed to Him of His attributes is in the manner befitting His majesty. For the spirit, which is some of His servants, is described as ascending when a person sleeps and prostrating beneath the Throne. Yet it is still in the body of its owner and has not completely departed from it. The person in his sleep senses the actions of his spirit affecting his body. So this ascent by which the spirit is described is not like the ascent of perceptible things. For when they ascend to a place, they depart completely from the first place, and their movement upward is a movement of transition from one place. But the spirit's ascent and prostration are not like that. End of quotation.

**Section**

One of the researchers who investigated the discussions of the modern scholars concerning the spirit wrote something of this sort: The theory of the spiritualists (*al-ruhiyyin*), which they argue for in Europe today by sensory evidence, is that the human being has a spirit that descended upon him from the higher assembly (*al-mala' al-a'la*). The intellect cannot reach the comprehension of its essence. It is connected to this clay body by means of a subtle, transparent vehicle shaped exactly like the body. But it is not of the body's nature nor governed by its laws. It is like a covering for the divine secret called the spirit. Perhaps this resembles the statement of Imam Malik ibn Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the spirit: "It is a form like the body." They say: the spirit and this covering (p. 3991) depart from the body at the occurrence of death for the person, to another world other than this world. But they do not separate from it completely; rather, the spirits of the dead are dispersed around us in every direction. Yet we do not see them with our eyes, because our eyes are not prepared for that, just as they are not prepared to see X-rays (Röntgen rays), although they exist, as the device made for it indicates. Its applications have entered the science of medicine and have given the natural science a great benefit. But there are some persons who have a special readiness for it, who see the spirits as passing vapor, and on their right and their left, with a real vision. End of summary.

**Note:** All of what we have presented is based on the premise that the intended meaning of "the spirit" (*al-ruh*) in the verse is the spirit of the human being.

Ibn al-Qayyim said in his book *al-Ruh* (The Soul): On this there is disagreement between the early scholars (al-salaf) and the later ones (al-khalaf). The majority of the salaf, indeed all of them, hold that the rūḥ asked about in the verse is not the souls of the children of Adam. Rather, it is the rūḥ that God mentions in His Book, which will stand on the Day of Resurrection together with the angels, and it is a great angel. It is firmly established in the Sahih from ʿAbdullah (Ibn Masʿud), who said: "While I was walking with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the stony ground of Madina, and he was leaning on a palm-stalk, we passed by a group of Jews. Some of them said to others: 'Ask him about the rūḥ.' Others said: 'Do not ask him, lest he tell you something you dislike.' Others said: 'Let us ask him.' A man stood up and said: 'O Abu l-Qasim! What is the rūḥ?' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) remained silent, so I knew he was receiving revelation, and I stood up. When it had cleared from him, he recited: ﴿And they ask you about the rūḥ...﴾, the verse." It is known that they asked him about a matter that can only be known through revelation. That rūḥ is the one with God that people do not know. As for the souls of the children of Adam, they are not among the unseen (al-ghayb). Groups of people, from the adherents of the religions and others, have spoken about them, but the answer concerning them did not come from the great prophetic figures.

If it is said: Abu l-Shaykh narrated from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Quraysh sent ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt and ʿAbdullah ibn Umayya ibn al-Mughira to the Jews of Madina to ask them about the Prophet (ﷺ). They said: 'A man has emerged among us who claims to be a prophet, and he is not upon our religion or yours.' They said: 'Who has followed him?' They said: 'Our lowly ones, the weak, the slaves, and those with no good in them. As for the nobles of his people, they have not followed him.' They said: 'The time of a prophet who is to emerge has drawn near, and he is as you describe this man's affair. So go to him and ask him about three matters, and your affair is with them. If he informs you of them, he is a truthful prophet; and if he does not inform you of them, he is a liar. Ask him about the rūḥ that God breathed into Adam. If he says to you that it is from God, then say: How does God punish in the Fire something that is from Him? He asked Gabriel about it, and God revealed the verse.' He said: It is a creature among the creatures of God, not from God."

It is said: Such an isnad cannot be used as evidence, for it is from the tafsir of al-Suddi from Abu Malik, and it contains unacceptable matters. The context of this story in the question, in the sound and musnad collections, all contradicts the context in al-Suddi's narration. al-Aʿmash and al-Mughira narrated it from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqama, from ʿAbdullah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a gathering of Jews while I was walking with him. They asked him about the rūḥ. He remained silent, so I thought he was receiving revelation, and then this came down: ﴿And they ask you about the rūḥ﴾." He meant the Jews: ﴿Say: The rūḥ is of the command of my Lord...﴾, the verse. It is the same in the recitation of ʿAbdullah. They said: "Thus we find something similar in the Torah: that the rūḥ is of the command of God, Mighty and Majestic." This was narrated by Jarir ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid and others, from al-Mughira. Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him about the rūḥ. The Prophet (ﷺ) did not answer them with anything. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the verse." This indicates the weakness of the hadith of al-Suddi, and that the question took place in Makka. For this hadith and the hadith of Ibn Masʿud clearly state that the question was asked directly by the Jews in Madina. Had the question and answer taken place earlier in Makka, the Prophet (ﷺ) would not have remained silent, but would have hastened to answer them with what had preceded of God's informing him and what God had revealed to him. The narrations from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning the interpretation of this verse are in extreme confusion. Either the fault lies with the narrators, or his own statements were confused on the matter. Then Ibn al-Qayyim cited the narrations from him with their chains, then said: The rūḥ in the Qur'an has several aspects:

First: revelation, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a rūḥ of Our command﴾ [al-Shura: 52], and His saying: ﴿He casts the rūḥ of His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 15]. He called revelation a rūḥ because life of hearts and spirits is achieved through it.

Second: the strength, steadfastness, and support with which He strengthens whomever He wills of His believing servants, as He said: ﴿Those, He has written faith into their hearts and supported them with a rūḥ from Himself﴾ [al-Mujadila: 22].

Third: Gabriel, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 193] ﴿upon your heart﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 194], and He said: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, then indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by God's permission﴾ [al-Baqara: 97]. He is the Rūḥ al-Qudus (the Holy Spirit), as He said: ﴿Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [al-Nahl: 102].

Fourth: the rūḥ about which the Jews asked, and they were answered that it is of the command of God. It has been said that it is the rūḥ mentioned in His saying: ﴿The day the rūḥ and the angels stand in ranks, they will not speak﴾ [al-Naba': 38], and that it is the rūḥ mentioned in His saying: ﴿The angels and the rūḥ descend therein by the permission of their Lord﴾ [al-Qadr: 4].

Fifth: the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary. He said, Exalted is He: ﴿The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, is only the messenger of God and His word which He cast to Mary, and a rūḥ from Him﴾ [al-Nisa': 171]. As for the souls of the children of Adam, their name in the Qur'an is only ever given as nafs (self/soul), as He said: ﴿O soul at peace﴾ [al-Fajr: 27], and He said: ﴿Nor do I swear by the self-reproaching soul﴾ [al-Qiyama: 2], and He said: ﴿Indeed the soul is ever inciting to evil﴾ [Yusuf: 53], and He said: ﴿Bring forth your souls﴾ [al-An'am: 93], and He said: ﴿And a soul and He who proportioned it﴾ [al-Shams: 7] ﴿and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness﴾ [al-Shams: 8], and He said: ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 57].

As for the Sunna, it came with the words nafs and rūḥ. End of quotation.

Ibn Kathir said: The narration of ʿAbdullah in the Sahih cited above suggests, at first glance, that this verse is Madani, and that it was revealed when the Jews asked him about that in Madina, although the whole surah is Makki. This may be answered by saying that it may have been revealed to him in Madina a second time, just as it was revealed to him in Makka before that; or that revelation came to him that he should answer them with the verse mentioned earlier that was revealed to him, namely this verse: ﴿And they ask you about the rūḥ﴾. End of quotation.

It has been narrated by Ibn Jarir from Qatada that the rūḥ in the verse is Gabriel, peace be upon him, and he transmitted this from Ibn ʿAbbas.

I say: What appears to me to be definite in the verse, given its preceding and following context, is that the rūḥ means the revelation of the Qur'an. This is close to the view of Qatada. The reason it is definite is that this verse is in the context of mentioning the Qur'an, its descent, and the favour of its being a healing and a mercy, and God, Exalted is He, has called revelation of the Qur'an a rūḥ. He said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a rūḥ of Our command﴾ [al-Shura: 52], and He said: ﴿He casts the rūḥ of His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 15]. So when they heard the rūḥ and declared their faith in it, they would pursue questions about it, out of disbelief that it could be from Him, glorified is He, and that a human like them could be sent with His command, so that He might make clear to them that it is a revelation He revealed, a rūḥ from Him and a casting from His command. A parallel to this verse is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They ask one another about what?﴾ [al-Naba': 1] ﴿About the great news﴾ [al-Naba': 2] ﴿about which they differ﴾ [al-Naba': 3], meaning: some of them deny it and some of them doubt its truth. This is because they are an ignorant people, with no acquaintance with knowledge and insights, let alone revelation and the properties of prophethood, due to the widespread illiteracy and ignorance among them, as is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾, meaning: of what your senses can grasp and your intelligence can reach. It is, in comparison with the countless things known, no more than a drop from the sea or a grain from the sand-dune. The principle is that the Qur'an is interlinked in its parts, explaining one part by another.

All that the earlier scholars mentioned, other than what we have mentioned, accords with what the noble verse can bear. Likewise the narration of Ibn Masʿud that they were answered with it, since it has aspects of meaning, and among them is what they asked about, so they were silenced by it. And God, Glorified and Exalted, knows best.

Then He, Exalted is He, pointed to His favour in what He revealed of this descent and the guidance through it, in His saying, glorified is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 17, verse 86:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[86] ﴿And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you; then you would not find for yourself concerning it any advocate against Us.﴾

﴿And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you﴾ i.e., of the Qur'an, which is a healing and a mercy for the believers. He expressed it by the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) to magnify its status, to describe it by what lies within the relative clause (al-silah), and to inform that it is not of the category of the speech of created beings. ﴿Then you would not find for yourself concerning it any advocate against Us﴾ i.e., anyone who would take it upon himself to restore it against Us.

(p-3996)

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He:

[87] ﴿Except as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed, His bounty upon you has been great.﴾

﴿Except as a mercy from your Lord﴾: i.e., but a mercy from your Lord has left it, not willing that it be taken away, but rather has taken charge of its preservation.

Al-Zamakhshari said: This is a favour (imtinan) from God, exalted is He, in the preservation of the Qur'an intact, after the great favour of its revelation and its safeguarding. So every person of knowledge must not be heedless of these two favours and must give thanks for them. They are God's favour upon him in preserving knowledge and its firm establishment in his breast, and His favour upon him in the continuance of what is preserved. ﴿Indeed, His bounty upon you has been great﴾: i.e., His bestowing upon you revelation, divine instruction, and selection for the messengership.

Then God, exalted is He, commanded him to address those polytheists who did not comprehend the worth of the revelation, and that it is a divine inspiration, with His saying:

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[88] ﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn were to gather together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to be aides to one another."﴾

﴿Say: "If mankind and the jinn gathered﴾, i.e., came to agreement, ﴿to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to be aides to one another"﴾, i.e., helpers. In the failure of the strength of all of them to do that, despite the length of time, is a decisive proof that it is not of the kind that is customary for humans to produce, but rather it is the speech of the Knower of the Unseen and the Witnessed.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[89] ﴿And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example, but most of the people refused except disbelief.﴾

﴿And We have certainly diversified﴾ means: We repeated, reiterated, and clarified. ﴿for the people in this Qur'an from every example﴾ (p-٣٩٩٧) means: from every meaning, which is like an example in its strangeness and beauty, so that it would be established and firmly rooted in their souls, and so that they would increase in reflection (tadabbur) and submission. But their condition was the opposite, for they only increased in disbelief, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿but most of the people refused except disbelief﴾, meaning: denial (juhud).

When the inimitability (i'jaz) of the Qur'an became clear, and that it is the greatest sign, and the proof was binding upon them and they were overcome, they began to make excuses by demanding signs, in the manner of one who is stunned, confounded by the proof, and stumbling in the skirts of bewilderment, concerning what He, exalted is He, related of them with His saying:

**The Commentary on His Words, Exalted Is He (ta'wil, interpretation):**

﴿They said, "We will not believe you until you make a spring gush forth for us from the earth,"﴾ meaning: until you split open for us springs from the land of Makkah.

﴿Or until you have a garden of date palms and grapevines, and you cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly﴾ [al-Isra' 17:91], meaning: a garden made of them. They put forward this proposal in their obstinacy because they used to travel to the lands of al-Sham and Iraq and saw the gardens and rivers there.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) related, in what he transmitted, that they said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "You know that no one among the people is more restricted in land, less wealthy, or harder pressed in living than we are. So ask your Lord, who sent you with what He sent you with, to remove these mountains that have closed in on us, to spread out our land for us, and to make rivers gush forth in it like the rivers of al-Sham and Iraq." Then they increased their demands and said:

﴿Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed﴾ [al-Isra' 17:92], meaning: in fragments as a punishment; ﴿or you bring God and the angels before us as a guarantee﴾ [al-Isra' 17:92], meaning: as a surety for what you say, a witness to its truth.

﴿Or you have a house of gold﴾ [al-Isra' 17:93], meaning: of gold; ﴿or you ascend into the sky. The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[94] ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them, except that they said: "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾

﴿And nothing prevented the people﴾, i.e., those whose obstinacy He has related, ﴿from believing when the guidance came to them, except that they said: "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ — i.e., except their amazement at the sending of a man as a messenger, meaning their denial that the messenger could be of the kind of humankind. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We have revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people, and give good news to those who have believed that they will have a sure standing with their Lord"?﴾ [Yunus: 2], and the verses on this are many. Then He, exalted is He, drew attention to His kindness and mercy toward His servants, that He sends to them a messenger of their own kind, so that they may understand from him and comprehend what he says, and be able to address him and converse with him. Even if the earth were a settled place for His angels, their messengers would be from among them, in keeping with the requirement of wisdom.

So He, glorified is He, said:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[95] ﴿Say: "If there were in the earth angels walking about securely, We would have sent down upon them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."﴾

﴿Say: "If there were in the earth angels walking about"﴾ — that is, on their feet, as mankind walks; ﴿securely﴾ — that is, dwelling in the earth, settled in it; ﴿We would have sent down upon them from the heaven an angel as a messenger﴾ — that is, of their own kind, to teach them what is good and guide them to the paths of right conduct. And since you are humans, We sent to you messengers from among you, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿As We have sent among you a messenger from among you, reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom and teaching you that which you did not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 151].

Admonition:

In the verse there is an indication of the need of one who dwells in the earth for the Message. The mercy and care of the Creator, may He be exalted, have decreed this; so He bestowed favour upon creation through the messengers, and completed their need through the Seal of His prophets. He rescued them from bewilderment, freed them from confusion, and brought them out from darkness into light.

The discussion of the words of Allah, the Exalted:

[96] ﴿Say: "Allah suffices as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever Acquainted with and Seeing of His servants."﴾

﴿Say: "Allah suffices as a witness between me and you"﴾ — that is, as witness that I have conveyed what I was sent with to you, and that you have denied and obstinately opposed it. Al-Razi (Fakhr al-Din al-Razi) affirmed that what is meant by the testimony is the testimony to his prophethood, peace be upon him, through the inimitability (i'jaz) of the Qur'an. That is: Allah's honouring me with this inimitable miracle suffices as a witness to my truthfulness. Whoever Allah testifies to be truthful is truthful. Therefore your saying, O polytheists, after this, that the Messenger should be an angel, is a corrupt arbitrary demand.

Abu al-Su'ud (Abu al-Su'ud al-Imadi) objected to him that what he established is not supported by the words of Allah, "between me and you," nor by what follows of the reasoning. Then Abu al-Su'ud said: "He did not say 'between us' only to confirm the separation and to make the opposition clear." The words of Allah, "Indeed, He is ever Acquainted with and Seeing of His servants," mean: He is Knowing of their conditions, so He will requite them. This is a consolation to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and a warning to the disbelievers.

(p-4002)

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[97] ﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the one guided; and whomever He sends astray, you will not find for them protectors other than Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; whenever it subsides, We increase them in blaze.﴾

﴿Whomever Allah guides﴾ means: to the truth, through what came from Him, to guidance. ﴿He is the one guided﴾ [al-Kahf: 17], and ﴿whomever He sends astray﴾ means: He creates misguidance in him through his own bad choice, like these obstinate people. ﴿You will not find for them protectors other than Him﴾ means: helpers who would guide them and protect them from His subjugation. The plural pronoun in (lahum, "for them") is used in agreement with the meaning of (man, "whoever"), while the singular is used in what precedes it, in agreement with the wording of (man). The secret of the difference between the two opposites is the indication of the unity of the path of truth and the scarcity of its travellers, and the multiplicity of the ways of misguidance and the abundance of the misguided. ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces﴾ means: they will be dragged upon them, like His saying: ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces﴾ [al-Qamar: 48].

Al-Qashani said: that is, with their heads lowered, because they are pulled toward the lower direction! ﴿And upon their existences and their essences that they had in the world.﴾ Like His saying: "As you live, you will die, and as you die, you will be resurrected." For (the face, al-wajh) is used to express the existing essence together with all its accidents and necessary attributes. That is, in the first state, without increase or decrease. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿blind, mute, and deaf﴾ means: just as they were in the world, not seeing the truth clearly and not speaking it, and feigning deafness to hearing it; so they, in the Hereafter, are likewise: they do not see what would delight their eyes, do not hear what would please their ears, and do not speak anything that would be accepted from them. ﴿And whoever is blind in this world, he will be blind in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Isra': 72]. Thus it is in al-Kashshaf (by al-Zamakhshari).

﴿Their refuge is Hell; whenever it subsides﴾ means: its blaze has calmed, after it has consumed their skins and their flesh. ﹫﴿We increase them in blaze﴾ means: in intensity; by replacing their skins and flesh, so that they return blazing and flaming.

(p-4003) Al-Zamakhshari said: It is as if, when they denied the return after annihilation, Allah made their recompense that He gave the Fire power over their parts, consuming them and annihilating them, and then He restores them. They remain in continual annihilation and restoration, so that this increases their regret over their denial of resurrection. And because it is more effective in exacting retribution from the one who denies.

And He indicated this by His saying:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[98] ﴿That is their recompense, because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, "When we are bones and crumbled dust, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾.

﴿That is their recompense, because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, "When we are bones and crumbled dust, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ That is: "Will we indeed be brought back to life in a new creation, by the return of the spirit into us, when our flesh has perished and we remain as bones?" Rather, our bones had become so thin that they turned into crumbled dust. Then Allah, exalted is He, argued against them and alerted them to His power to do that, by His saying:

The discussion of the Almighty's words:

[99] ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create their like? And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt. Yet the wrongdoers refuse except with disbelief.﴾

﴿Do they not see﴾ — i.e., do they not know: ﴿that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create their like﴾ — i.e., on the Day of Resurrection, producing them in another creation and returning them as He originated them. The meaning: they already know, by the evidence of reason, that whoever is able to create the heavens and the earth is able to create the likes of them from mankind, since they are not stronger in creation than these. As He said: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 27]. Nor is restoration harder for Him than initial origination; rather, it is easier.

Al-Shihab said: There is no need to make (mithl, "like") here a metonymy for them, as in the saying "your like does not withhold," although that is correct. If the creation of their like were taken as an expression for restoration, it would be better. ﴿And He has appointed for them a term (ajal) about which there is no doubt﴾ — i.e., He has appointed for their restoration and their raising from their graves a fixed term and a determined period that must come to an end, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And We delay it only for a counted term﴾ [Hud: 104]. ﴿Yet the wrongdoers refuse﴾ — i.e., after the proof has been established against them and the evidence made clear — ﴿except with disbelief﴾ — i.e., denial and persistence in their falsehood and misguidance.

A subtle point:

Al-Shihab said: This clause — "and He has appointed" etc. — is conjoined to the clause ﴿Do they not see﴾, because although it is in the form of an imperative/performative clause, it is interpreted as a declarative one, as in the "Sharh al-Kashshaf"; its meaning being: they already know by the indication of reason that He is able to resurrect and restore, ﴿and He has appointed for them﴾ — i.e., for their restoration — ﴿a term﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection; meaning, they know its possibility and the report of the Truthful One concerning it and His appointing a term for it, so it is obligatory to affirm it. Or [the meaning is]: He has appointed for them a term, which is death and the departure from life. It is not hidden from any intelligent person that He did not create them in vain, so they must be recompensed for what they did in this abode. Thus there is no sense in denial. The connection of the two conjoined clauses is thus clear, both in wording and meaning; and ﴿there is no doubt about it﴾ is evident on the second reading. On the first reading its meaning is: it should not be denied by one who reflects. It has also been said that it is conjoined to His saying ﴿creates﴾.

And the Almighty's words:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[100] ﴿Say: "Even if you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold them for fear of spending. And man is ever stingy."﴾

﴿Say: "Even if you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord"﴾ i.e., His provision and all His blessings upon His creation. ﴿then you would withhold them for fear of spending﴾ i.e., you would be stingy with them, fearing that they would be exhausted by spending, even though they never run out nor are depleted ever; because this is from your natures and dispositions. For this reason, He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿And man is ever stingy﴾, i.e., miserly.

(p-4005) Remarks:

The first: this verse reaches, in describing the idolaters with stinginess, the extreme that imagination cannot reach, as al-Zamakhshari said.

The second: what the end of the verse implies, that every person is stingy, is not applicable to the True Generous One, Glorified is He; because a person is either withholding or spending. The second only occurs for a purpose for the rational agent, either worldly, such as a material exchange, or immaterial, such as a good reputation, service, or enjoyment, as in spending on one's family. What is for a material exchange is a trade, not a giving freely. Or it is with regard to the majority, and treating others as if they were non-existent, as it was said:

"Count for us in our time, out of the tales of nobility,
Whoever spares people his evil, he is in the generosity of Hatim."

Al-Shihab reported this.

Ibn Kathir said: Allah Exalted describes man as such, insofar as he is man, except whom Allah has granted success and guidance; for stinginess, impatience, and anxiety are his attribute, as Allah Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, man was created anxious﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 19] ﴿when evil touches him, impatient﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 20] ﴿and when good touches him, withholding﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 21] ﴿except those who pray﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 22]. There are many similar examples in the Noble Qur'an.

The third: He mentioned this verse after what precedes it, to establish His exclusive possession of the treasuries of mercy and the vastness of His generosity, bounty, and kindness, just as He alone possesses that dazzling power of creating the heavens and the earth, so that His great power and the vastness of His full treasuries may become clear to them, and thereby they reach certainty of the truth of what the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, claimed, and of the validity of what he calls them to.

This meaning was expressed in the style of explaining what man was created upon, as a reminder to him of his deficiency and weakness, his anxiety and greed; so that he knows that he was not created in vain, left to himself to pursue whatever his soul and desire demand. The meaning is: Will you not take heed of the vastness of His mercy and the generality of His favor, and of what proves His oneness in His divinity, (p-4006) and do you not see what you are upon, that if you possessed what has no end of His treasuries, you would be stingy with them? This indicates that He is the Owner of dominion, and that you are subjected to His command! This verse is like His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Or do they have a share of the dominion? Then they would not give people even a speck﴾ [al-Nisa: 53], i.e., if they had a share in Allah's dominion, they would not give anyone anything, not even the amount of a speck. It has come in the two Sahihs: "The hand of Allah is full; spending does not diminish it, ever flowing by night and day. Have you considered what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? For it has not decreased what is in His right hand."

And His words, Exalted is He:

**The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:**

[101] ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs. So ask the Children of Israel, when he came to them, and Pharaoh said to him, "I truly think you, O Moses, are bewitched."﴾

﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs﴾, evident in their indication of the truth of what Allah sent him with. Their discussion has already passed in Surah al-A'raf, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾ [al-A'raf: 133], and so on. ﴿So ask the Children of Israel﴾, meaning about them, for they know them from what they have of the Torah. Thus the truthfulness of you (Muhammad, ﷺ) becomes manifest to the polytheists, and the believer's heart in you grows in tranquility, because when the proofs converge, that is stronger and more established. ﴿When he came to them, and Pharaoh said to him, "I truly think you, O Moses, are bewitched."﴾ That is, he went to Pharaoh, displayed his signs, and invited him to believe in Allah, exalted is He, and to send the Children of Israel with him. Pharaoh then said what he said.

As for His saying ﴿مَسْحُورًا﴾ (bewitched), it may mean "you have been bewitched, so your mind has been confused"; or it may mean "a sorcerer," in the sense of attribution; or it may be literal, and this fits with the staff turning into a serpent. According to the first meaning, it is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is surely a madman﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 27].

(p-٤٠٠٧)

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[102] ﴿He said: "Certainly you know that none has sent down these but the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear proofs. And indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed."﴾

﴿He said, "Certainly you know"﴾ i.e., O Pharaoh. ﴿that none has sent down these﴾ i.e., the nine signs. ﴿but the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear proofs﴾ i.e., manifest and evident proofs, not magic or illusion. But you are obstinate and arrogant. Similar to this is His saying: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance﴾ [al-Naml: 14]. And (al-basa'ir) is the plural of basir in the sense of mubsira, i.e., evident. Or the intended meaning is the proofs, treating them as if they were insights of the intellects. It may also mean lessons (ibra): ﴿And indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed﴾ i.e., destroyed.

The discussion of the words of Allah the Exalted:

[103-104] ﴿So he (Pharaoh) resolved to drive them out of the land, but We drowned him and those with him, all together.﴾ ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth in a mixed multitude."﴾ [al-Isra': 104].

﴿So he resolved﴾ i.e., Pharaoh. ﴿To drive them out of the land﴾ i.e., to frighten and unsettle them, with what would move them to flee lightly out of fear of him, or to expel them from the face of the earth by killing and extermination. The pronoun refers to Musa and his people. And "the land" is the land of Egypt, or the land which He had permitted them to journey to and dwell in, namely Palestine. As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿We drowned him and those with him, all together﴾, i.e., the evil of his scheme recoiled upon him, because he pursued them with his armies after He had permitted them to travel from Egypt to Palestine, in order to return them to his servitude; so Allah the Exalted destroyed him and his armies by drowning.

﴿And We said after him﴾ [al-Isra': 104] i.e., after his drowning: ﴿to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land"﴾ [al-Isra': 104], which is the land of Canaan, the country of their father Israel, which they had been promised.

(p-4008) Ibn Kathir said: In this is a glad tiding to the Prophet (ﷺ) of the conquest of Makkah, even though the surah is Meccan, revealed before the Hijrah. And so it happened, for the people of Makkah resolved to expel the Messenger from it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed they almost drove you out of the land to expel you from it﴾ [al-Isra': 76]. For this reason Allah made His Messenger inherit Makkah, and he entered it by force, according to the more well-known of the two opinions, and subdued its people, then released them out of forbearance and generosity. Just as Allah made the people who were oppressed among the Children of Israel inherit the eastern and western parts of the earth, and made them inherit the lands of Pharaoh and his wealth, his crops, his fruits and his treasures, as He said: ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 59]. And He said here: ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land"﴾ [al-Isra': 104]. And His words, the Exalted: ﴿But when the promise of the Hereafter comes﴾ [al-Isra': 104], i.e., the establishment of the Hour: ﴿We will bring you forth in a mixed multitude﴾ [al-Isra': 104], i.e., a gathering in which you and your enemies are mingled together. Then He will judge between you and distinguish between your blessed and your wretched. Then the Exalted purified the sanctuary of the Qur'an from being a fabrication, and explained its containing what suits the natural disposition and corresponds to reality, by His words, the Exalted:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 17, verses 105–106:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[105–106] ﴿And with the truth We have sent it down, and with the truth it has descended. And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And [it is] a Qur'an which We have separated [in revelation] that you might recite it to the people over a long period. And We have sent it down, progressively.﴾ [al-Isra' 17:106]

﴿And with the truth We have sent it down﴾ means: in reality We have sent it down as a Book from Us, so where are you going? As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you. He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:166]. ﴿And with the truth it has descended﴾ means: accompanied by the truth, which is the stability of the order of the world in its most perfect forms. This is what it comprises of beliefs, rulings, noble morals, and everything that opposes falsehood, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it﴾ [Fussilat 41:42]. ﴿And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾. ﴿And [it is] a Qur'an which We have separated﴾ [al-Isra' 17:106] means: We sent it down in separated, gradual parts. It is also read with the doubled letter (faraqnahu, with tashdid). The two readings have the same meaning. ﴿That you might recite it to the people over a long period﴾ [al-Isra' 17:106] means: at a measured pace, with deliberation and steadiness, for it is easier for memorization and more helpful for understanding. ﴿And We have sent it down, progressively﴾ [al-Isra' 17:106] means: from Us, according to circumstances and interests.

The two readings have the same meaning. ﴿That you might recite it to the people over a long period﴾ [al-Isra' 17:106] means: at a measured pace, with deliberation and steadiness, for it is easier for memorization and more helpful for understanding. ﴿And We have sent it down, progressively﴾ [al-Isra' 17:106] means: from Us, according to circumstances and interests.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[107-109] "Say: Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces in prostration, and they say, 'Exalted is our Lord; indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.' And they fall down upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility."

"Say: Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces in prostration" and "they say, 'Exalted is our Lord; indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled'" and "they fall down upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility."

al-Zamakhshari said: This is a command to turn away from them, to disdain them, to look down upon their affair, and not to be concerned with them, with their faith, or with their refusal of it. And if they do not enter into faith and do not affirm the Qur'an, while they are people of ignorance (jahiliyyah) and polytheism, there are those better and more excellent than them, namely the scholars who read the Books and knew what revelation and the sacred laws are. They have believed in it and affirmed it, and it was established for them that he is the Arab Prophet promised in their Books. When it is recited to them, they fall down in prostration and glorify God, magnifying His command and His fulfilment of what He promised in the revealed Books, and what He gave good news of concerning the sending of Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and the sending down of the Qur'an upon him. This is what is meant by the promise in His saying: "the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled" [17:108].

If you ask: What is the explanation of "Indeed, those who were given knowledge"? Is it a reason for what? I say: It may be a reason for His saying "Believe in it or do not believe," and it may be a reason for "Say" by way of consolation to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and to comfort his heart. As if it were said: Be consoled regarding the faith of the ignorant by the faith of the scholars. And according to the first: "If you do not believe in it, [then] indeed there has believed in it one who is better than you."

If you ask: What is the meaning of falling down upon the chin? I say: It is falling upon the face. The chin was mentioned, which is the meeting-place of the two jaws, because the one prostrating first meets the earth with the chin of his face. If you ask: The preposition of elevation (ʿalā) is apparent in meaning, when you say "he fell upon his face and upon his chin," so what is the meaning of the preposition lām in "fell for his chin and for his face"? He said: [the poet's line] "So he fell prostrate for the two hands and for the mouth." I say: Its meaning is that he made his chin and his face ready for falling, and he specified it with this because the lām indicates specification.

If you ask: Why did he repeat "fall down upon the chins"? I say: Because of the difference of the two states: their falling while in the state of prostrating, and their falling while in the state of weeping. End of quotation.

Admonition:

The description of these people and their praise for falling down weeping indicates the recommendation of weeping and humble submission. For every praiseworthy quality and attribute by which God the Exalted describes those among His servants whom He loves, it is necessary to adopt it; and whatever blameworthy quality He condemns in them, which He detests, must be avoided.

Al-Imam al-Ghazali, in *al-Ihya'*, counted weeping among the outward etiquettes of recitation. He said: Weeping is recommended along with the recitation. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: "Recite the Qur'an and weep; and if you do not weep, then feign weeping." Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: When you recite the prostration of Subhan (17), do not hasten to prostrate until you weep; and if the eye of one of you does not weep, then let his heart weep. The way to force weeping is to bring sorrow to the heart, for from sorrow weeping arises. The way to bring sorrow is to reflect upon what it contains of threat, warning, covenants and pledges; then to reflect upon one's shortcoming in His commands and prohibitions, so he will inevitably grieve and weep. If sorrow and weeping do not come to him, as they come to the people of pure hearts, then let him weep over the loss of sorrow and weeping, for that is the greatest of calamities. End of quotation.

al-Suyuti mentioned in *al-Iklil* that al-Shafi'i used as evidence His saying, exalted is He: "and they say, 'Exalted is our Lord'" [17:108], etc., for the recommendation of this remembrance in the prostration of recitation.
